title: Eurostar cancels Paris-London trains after staff go on unannounced strike
summary: Eurostar has canceled several trains between Paris and London due to an unannounced strike by some staff
story: Eurostar has canceled several trains between Paris and London due to an unannounced strike by some staff
PARIS -- Several Eurostar trains between Paris and London scheduled for Wednesday are being canceled because of a strike by some Paris-based staff that the company said it was notified of overnight.
Eurostar advised travelers to postpone their journeys and warned of possible disruption on other routes.

“Regrettably, Eurostar customers travelling between Paris and London today are being impacted by industrial action which the company was notified of overnight," the company said in a statement. “Unfortunately, this is causing some cancellations to services. Other routes are not directly affected but may see some knock-on impact.”

The striking staff include train drivers and managers based in Paris, Eurostar said. It advised customers whose trains had been canceled not to go to the station, saying they could rebook for another date or receive a full refund.
“Discussions are ongoing with the union and the company remains open and willing to engage in constructive dialogue,” Eurostar said.
Eurostar operates passenger trains linking London with Paris and other European destinations.

title: Large explosion reported at a major oil facility in the Thai capital
summary: An explosion and fire at a major oil facility in Bangkok injures at least nine people and forces nearby residents to evacuate briefly
story: An explosion and fire at a major oil facility in Bangkok injures at least nine people and forces nearby residents to evacuate briefly
BANGKOK -- An explosion and fire at a major oil facility in the Thai capital on Thursday injured at least nine people and forced nearby residents to briefly evacuate, authorities said.

Most of the injured suffered burns and three people were in critical condition, according to Erawan Medical Center in Bangkok. Video posted on social media showed thick black smoke rising from the site in an eastern neighborhood of Bangkok.

A mobile phone alert sent to residents said the incident happened around 3 p.m. and advised people to avoid the area. The city authority reported less than an hour later that the ensuing fire was put out.
Officials later said nearby residents can return home, but advised those living in a 5-kilometer (3-mile) radius of the facility to be cautious of air pollution.
The Pollution Control Department said it sent officials to assess air and water quality in the surrounding area.

Bangchak Corp., which owns the refining and storage facility, confirmed the fire in a Facebook post and said that the cause was still being investigated. The company also said it has halted all production operations.

Energy Minister Akanat Promphan said the fire appeared to start at one of the refinery units, which is about 100 meters (330 feet) away from the oil storage. He said he would inspect the site to ensure there's no further risk.
“If we're not a hundred percent certain that the oil storage is safe, we won't allow them to resume operations,” he said.
Akanat said Thailand's oil supply should not be affected, as there are five other refineries in the country and this facility is not among the biggest.
The refinery, with a listed capacity of 120,000 barrels a day, is the fifth biggest in Thailand and the only one situated in an urban area.
An explosion and fire at the refinery in July 2012 caused damage in a nearby residential neighborhood and it took two weeks to repair the facility.

title: South Korea's central bank raises key interest rate to fight inflation
summary: South Korea’s central bank has raised its benchmark interest rate for the third time since July
story: South Korea’s central bank has raised its benchmark interest rate for the third time since July

SEOUL, South Korea -- South Korea’s central bank on Thursday raised its benchmark interest rate for the third time since July, aiming to tighten money supply in the face of inflationary pressure driven by the war in the Middle East and the country’s booming semiconductor exports fueled by global demand related to artificial intelligence.

In raising its policy rate by a quarter-percentage point to 3.25%, the Bank of Korea also lifted its growth forecast for South Korea’s economy to 3.9% from 3.3% for 2026, and to 4.1% from 2.9% for 2027, following months of strong exports.

Despite the robust performance in trade, analysts have noted that consumer spending has remained subdued due to rising prices, stagnant wages and the burden of servicing South Korea’s notoriously high household debt.

Consumer prices rose 2.8% in October from a year earlier, above the bank’s 2% target. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices to better gauge underlying price pressures, rose 2.7% over the same period.

The bank said in a statement that raising borrowing costs was necessary as inflation was expected to remain above target for a “considerable period” and also cited “persistent risks on the side of financial stability.”

The bank said the global economy was maintaining modest growth despite the conflict in the Middle East, mainly driven by AI-related investments, but price pressures would continue to grow, driven by increasing energy costs.

It warned that the rising house prices in the capital Seoul and the metropolitan area could further aggravate the country’s household debt, which reached an all-time high of 2,030 trillion won ($1.51 trillion) as of the third quarter, nearing the size of the country's annual gross domestic product, according to the bank’s data. Shin Hyun Song, the bank’s governor, said household borrowing is continuing to rise amid expectations of further home price increases in the greater capital area, making it necessary for policymakers to “remain vigilant regarding the risks of financial imbalances.” He said the rate hike was also a preemptive move to curb inflationary pressures and that consumer prices are expected to remain above the bank’s target until sometime in 2028. Shin said it would take time for the country’s export gains to translate into meaningful increases in consumers’ spending capacities and that the bank’s tight monetary policy should be complemented by fiscal measures to ease the burden on households.
The bank’s decision to raise the policy rate was not a unanimous decision, with two of the seven members of its monetary policy committee arguing to keep the rate at 3%.

title: Global stocks rise and tech shares rebound as US closes for Thanksgiving
summary: Shares have advanced in Europe and Asia while U.S. markets are closed for the Thanksgiving holiday
story: Shares have advanced in Europe and Asia while U.S. markets are closed for the Thanksgiving holiday
HONG KONG -- Shares advanced in Europe and Asia on Thursday while U.S. markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.
Buying of stocks tied to artificial intelligence helped push benchmarks in Asia higher, though some profit-taking by investors toward the end of the day pared those gains.

Investors have been growing cautious about the AI trade. They also are watching for impacts from the latest tariff hikes Washington plans to impose on China, Japan, the European Union and other trading partners.
In early European trading, Germany's DAX jumped 1.9% to 25,180.12, while France's CAC 40 climbed 1.8% to 8,126.47. Britain's FTSE 100 added 1.6% to 10,591.83.
U.S. stock futures also climbed, with the S&P 500 futures up 0.5%. U.S. markets will reopen Friday for a holiday-shortened session.

In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rebounded and closed 0.9% higher at 57,499.16. OpenAI investor SoftBank Group jumped 7.3%, while memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings surged 12.6%. Shares of chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron were up 0.6%.
South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index added 0.3% to 4,711.21 after a 6.2% drop a day earlier. Samsung Electronics gained 0.4%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix rose 2.2%.
Taiwan’s Taiex was 2.5% higher. But shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., edged 0.2% lower.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index was 1.2% higher at 22,226.88. The Shanghai Composite index was up less than 0.1% at 3,476.88.
Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.8% to 8,763.80.
India’s Sensex rose 0.5%.

Wall Street closed mixed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The benchmark S&P 500 index lost 0.3% Wednesday after falling as much as 3.2% earlier in the day. The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite closed 0.6% lower, after recovering from a drop of as much as 4.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average picked up 0.3%.

Nvidia fell 3.9% as AI shares lost steam for a second day after Jensen Huang’s comeback as CEO. On Wednesday, S&P Global Ratings warned it could downgrade Nvidia’s credit rating over concerns surrounding its management and governance.

Broadcom, which had fallen sharply earlier in the day, was 0.1% lower at the close. Anthropic, which began public trading last week, recovered from an early drop and ended 1.1% higher, though still below its IPO, or initial public offering, price of $83 per share.
In commodities trading, oil prices climbed early Thursday as tensions in the Middle East persisted even as global oil supply continued to recover.

Brent crude, the international standard, was 0.5% higher at $91.09 per barrel. It was trading at approximately $72 a barrel before the war began in late February. Benchmark U.S. crude gained 1% to $84.51 per barrel.

Recent reports of vessels being targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global oil transport, have contributed to concerns over oil flows and “brought supply risks back into focus,” ING commodities strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson said in a commentary Thursday.
The U.S. dollar rose to 159.30 Japanese yen from 159.16 yen. The euro was trading at $1.0968, down from $1.0974.

title: Malaysia Airlines’ parent to buy 10 Boeing Dreamliners, with options for 6 more
summary: Malaysia Airlines' parent company has announced plans to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with options for six more, as part of its fleet modernization strategy
story: Malaysia Airlines' parent company has announced plans to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with options for six more, as part of its fleet modernization strategy

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia -- Malaysia Airlines’ parent company unveiled plans Wednesday to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft, with options for six more, as part of its fleet modernization strategy and expansion into Europe.
The 16 are valued at $9.3 billion before discounts, Malaysia Aviation Group President and CEO Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said. Airlines typically get steep discounts when they buy in bulk.
He said the new planes would bolster the group's competitiveness and support its expansion into Europe.

The first deliveries of the 787-10 Dreamliners are scheduled to begin in 2032, with the initial 10 aircraft expected by 2035, MAG said in a statement. The wide-body aircraft would gradually replace the group's existing seven Airbus A350s, boosting fuel efficiency and providing greater capacity and operational flexibility, it said.
Nasaruddin said the group currently operates a fleet of about 101 aircraft and expects this to grow to 129 aircraft by 2035, including its cargo operations and low-cost airline Firefly.

The Dreamliners are expected to initially support Malaysia Airlines’ existing network, including services to London and Paris Charles de Gaulle, as well as Asia-Pacific, covering Sydney, Melbourne, Tokyo, Osaka and Seoul, he said.
“As we look ahead to the next phase of growth, these aircraft will strengthen our ability to serve key international markets with greater capacity, efficiency and flexibility,” he added.

title: Chinese consumer advocate stranded in South Korea amid a crackdown at homoe
summary: Consumer rights advocate Wang Hai is stranded in South Korea with his family after fleeing China fearing arrest during a crackdown on campaigners seeking compensation from businesses
story: Consumer rights advocate Wang Hai is stranded in South Korea with his family after fleeing China fearing arrest during a crackdown on campaigners seeking compensation from businesses

WASHINGTON -- Chinese consumer rights advocate Wang Hai has spent three decades exposing counterfeit goods and seeking compensation for buyers. In recent months, he left China fearing he was a target of the authorities, but now he is stranded in South Korea with his family, facing possible deportation home.

Wang, a well-known campaigner against counterfeit goods, said China invalidated his passport and South Korean authorities rejected his asylum. The United States also revoked his tourist visa, narrowing his options for leaving South Korea and deepening his fears of being sent back to China.

Chinese authorities launched a campaign against organized crime in July, saying they would target “malicious compensation claims.” Since then, authorities have arrested at least 100 people for allegedly extorting businesses through anti-counterfeiting work or consumer compensation claims, according to official statements reviewed by The Associated Press.
Wang said the arrests made him fear he could be next, prompting him to leave a country where official Chinese media had once praised him for his role as an anti-counterfeiting activist.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs told The Associated Press it was not aware of Wang’s case. The Ministry of Public Security did not respond to a request for comment.

The quagmire in which Wang, 53, and his family have found themselves has drawn concerns from rights advocates over China’s efforts to target critics abroad and the narrowing options for people seeking refuge in the U.S.

“The Chinese government’s practice of transnational repression is well documented, including in South Korea,” said Yaqiu Wang, senior China researcher at Human Rights Watch, based in Washington, and “there is no doubt that the Trump administration has created a far more hostile environment for immigrants, and even visitors.”
Wang spoke to the AP from South Korea about his situation and has appealed the rejection of his asylum application in that country.
The activist said that he arrived in South Korea in late September with his wife, 8-year-old daughter and infant son.

Wang said he believed Chinese authorities were targeting him and that dozens of his staff members were arrested and questioned. Some remain in detention, he said. One staffer had his passport revoked while traveling from Thailand to Singapore last month, he said.
“The very same job has suddenly morphed from being praised into something associated with organized crime — it’s absolutely surreal," said Wang.
Asked what he is afraid of if he is sent to China, Wang didn’t hesitate: “I would definitely spend the rest of my life behind bars.”

A notice reviewed by AP showed South Korean immigration authorities rejected Wang's and his family's applications for refugee status. AP also reviewed the U.S. Embassy email that revoked his visa, in which U.S. authorities told Wang that new information made him inadmissible to the U.S. or ineligible for a U.S. visa but did not provide specific details.
South Korea’s Justice Ministry said it couldn’t share any information, citing local laws on refugees and personal information protection.
Observers say that South Korea’s acceptance rate for refugee status applications has been less than 2% in recent years.
The U.S. State Department didn't respond to the request for comment.

Wang became a household name in China in the 1990s for exposing counterfeit goods, an increasingly widespread problem as the country’s market economy expanded rapidly and consumer protection oversight lagged.

In 1998, Wang joined a roundtable discussion with then-U.S. President Bill Clinton during his visit to Shanghai. Wang told Clinton he had been viewed as “immoral” at home, according to a White House transcript.

Chinese state media, however, largely portrayed him favorably, calling him “China’s No. 1 anti-counterfeiting activist.” Professional consumer advocates were compared to “woodpeckers,” rooting out problems in the marketplace.

Wang ran a rights-protection company in Beijing for about 30 years and a testing laboratory supporting anti-counterfeiting work for five years. He said both were forced to close after many of his staff, including three lawyers, were arrested in September.

The closure of his offices came after China launched its campaign against organized crime. Authorities said some people were using consumer complaints, lawsuits or threats of exposure to extort money from businesses through what officials called “malicious compensation claims.”
Some lawyers say consumer rights advocates play a positive role by exposing illegal practices, pressing businesses to address problems and helping authorities enforce regulations.

“The fact that some individuals engage in these activities as a profession or as a source of income does not invalidate the legitimacy of such social oversight itself,” said Zhang Yansheng, a Beijing-based lawyer.

Wang’s consumer advocacy began more than three decades ago, when he suspected two pairs of Sony headphones he bought at a Beijing department store were counterfeit. He bought the remaining 10 pairs and secured compensation of twice the purchase price. It was widely celebrated on Chinese state media as a pioneering case of consumer activism.
He went on to run his own company and testing lab, helping consumers seek compensation and pushing for stronger consumer protections.
Wang and other advocates also pushed for a minimum compensation payment of 500 yuan ($75) for consumers, a proposal later incorporated into a revised consumer protection law in 2013.

His most recent case involved helping cherry farmers in the northeastern city of Dalian get compensation after they bought fake pesticide. He said Dalian police later arrested and detained around four dozen people including the cherry farmers, two lawyers who represented the farmers, and Wang's staff.
Finally he fled China.

Wang said he has since focused on researching asylum options and hopes to settle in the U.S., Canada, Britain, Australia or New Zealand, seeking what he called “real law enforcement and freedom” to “get away from China's transnational repression.”
After his U.S. visa was revoked, Wang is seeking resettlement in Canada with the help of a human rights organization.

Fearing arrest by Chinese authorities even outside China, he said he and his family mostly stay indoors in South Korea. He said his bank accounts in China have been frozen, leaving the family in financial difficulty, and his 8-year-old daughter is struggling with her mental health because she cannot attend school.
AP writer Hyung-jin Kim in Seoul, South Korea, contributed to this report.

title: Here are the main issues driving Spain's national election
summary: Spain is to elect a new government on Sunday in a snap election that could unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez
story: Spain is to elect a new government on Sunday in a snap election that could unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez
MADRID -- MADRID (AP) — Spain will elect a new government on Sunday in a snap election that could unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

The progressive leader has governed Spain for 8 years, presiding over several crises, years of economic expansion and immigration-led population growth. No issue, however, has affected Spaniards during this time as much as unaffordable housing.
How Spaniards vote will determine Spain's positions on issues like immigration, with implications for Europe, which will see national elections in France, Italy and Poland in the next 12 months.
Here are the key issues driving the election.

Sánchez aimed to capitalize on the frustration that many Spaniards have around housing when he called early elections last month, hoping to frame the race around affordability issues traditionally favorable to his left-wing politics.
Rental and home costs have soared over the past decade in Spanish cities and tourist hotspots, and voters have said it's their top concern for over a year, according to the state pollster CIS.
Spain's housing crunch reflects similar pressures felt across Europe, where young people are battling cost of living crises in several countries and demanding solutions from governments.

Both Sánchez and his main opponent, conservative Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, have promised to enact measures to help first-time homebuyers if elected, and improve conditions for renters. Sánchez, whose government has tried to crack down on unauthorized tourist accommodations on platforms like Airbnb, has emphasized the need to regulate the housing market. Feijóo, on the other hand, has stressed the need for more construction, promising to build a million new homes over the next four years as prime minister.
Sánchez's immigration-friendly policies have made the 54-year-old leader an outlier in Europe amid a rise in far-right populism.

In recent years, Spain has taken in millions of people from Latin America and Africa, and Sánchez has defended his government's stance by citing the economic and social benefits that those who come to Spain legally bring to the eurozone’s fourth-largest economy.
Spain also legalized earlier this year the status of nearly 1.2 million immigrants who were already living in the country without proper documentation.

Feijóo and Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party that would likely join the PP in a coalition government, have advocated for tougher immigration policies. The campaign has coincided with a spike in migrants arriving on boats from Africa to Spain's Canary Islands.

Feijóo has promised stronger border management, while Abascal favors a much tougher approach. His party has advocated for mass deportations, restricting immigrants’ access to public services and prioritizing Spanish nationals.

For Europe, tougher migration controls in Spain would bring the country closer to Europe's center-right mainstream and could result in more cooperation on the deportation of migrants who arrive illegally.

Sánchez's Socialist party, including members of his inner circle, has been dogged by legal cases involving corruption. They have implicated a former minister and top officials as well as Sánchez's brother and wife — who denies wrongdoing.
Sánchez has likened the cases against his family to a smear campaign, but has apologized for proven corruption cases involving his former cohorts.
Well before the campaign, the prime minister's critics have said he is unfit to lead the country due to his party's corruption scandals. Sánchez has always maintained he was unaware of them.
Voters list corruption and bad behavior by politicians as a concern, but it factors lower than affordability issues, working conditions and immigration, according to the CIS survey.

Two fatal train accidents this year on Spain’s extensive high-speed rail network have put safety issues at the center of the election. Sánchez, whose transport minister resigned after the second crash, has stressed to voters that a right-wing government would cut social spending, which is necessary to maintain public services and the rail network.

Feijóo has excoriated Sánchez’s record, vowing to “return quality to public services” and conduct a rapid audit of the rail network within his first few months in office. His pitch to voters has largely centered on improving government management and the competence of public officials.

Spain's public healthcare system also ranks high among voter concerns, according to the CIS survey, and in the run-up to the election, Sánchez's government has pushed through a raft of social welfare spending.
Spain is highly exposed to natural disasters that are affected by climate change, including ferocious forest fires, long-term drought and sometimes deadly flash floods.
The country is also a leader in renewable energy, generating more than half its electricity from non-carbon sources, mainly from solar and wind.
Under Sánchez, Spain's government has pledged to generate all its energy from renewable sources by 2050 and to shut down the country's remaining nuclear reactors by 2035.
Feijóo says he would “realistically reformulate” Spain's climate commitments, while keeping nuclear power in the mix with renewables, energy storage and sufficient backup capacity.
Vox, like other far-right parties, has pushed climate skepticism. Its party leader Abascal has criticized the government's environmental agenda.

title: Argentina bans its central bank from printing money for the government
summary: Argentina’s Congress has approved a law that bans the central bank from printing money to cover government spending
story: Argentina’s Congress has approved a law that bans the central bank from printing money to cover government spending

BUENOS AIRES, Argentina -- Argentina’s Congress voted Thursday to bar the central bank from printing money to pay the government’s bills, enshrining in law a key pillar of President Javier Milei’s fight against the country’s notoriously high inflation.

Under the new charter, the central bank’s “primary and fundamental mission” will be to preserve the value of the peso — a goal Milei has pursued in office even though, as a candidate in 2023, he promised to abolish the bank and replace the local currency with the U.S. dollar.

The 141-0 vote in the Chamber of Deputies, with 99 abstentions, comes days after preliminary figures showed Argentina had likely slipped into recession, less than a year before the libertarian economist seeks a second four-year term.

For generations, when Argentine governments spent more than they collected in taxes, they turned to the central bank to print pesos to fill the gap, fueling repeated currency crises and bouts of hyperinflation. The law puts an end to “91 years of plunder, expropriation, impunity and institutional decay,” Milei’s office said in a statement.

The new charter bars the bank from lending to any level of government or otherwise financing the Treasury. It also scraps the bank's employment and economic development goals added under former President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, the Peronist opposition leader whose administrations leaned heavily on the central bank to fund unbridled spending.

But the law gives the monetary authority less protection than Milei sought. His original bill would have required a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress to remove the bank’s governor, his appointee Santiago Bausili. The Senate watered down that clause, and the lower house lacked the votes Thursday to restore it. Now a president can replace the bank’s leadership with a simple Senate majority.

Milei has slashed public spending in the past three years, turning Argentina's chronic fiscal deficits into a surplus and helping cut annual inflation from nearly 300% in early 2024 to 33% last month.

Yet Milei has been reluctant to let the market set Argentina’s most important price: the exchange rate. The charter leaves currency controls in the bank’s hands and sets no clear rule for how it should respond to inflation.

Tight monetary policy has kept the peso strong, making Argentine goods expensive abroad just as factories face a flood of cheaper imports. Oil and gas exports have boomed while labor-intensive industries like manufacturing, retail and construction have struggled.

Argentina’s economy shrank an estimated 1.8% in the third quarter, after a 0.6% contraction in the second, according to official data released Tuesday. Two straight quarters of decline is the usual definition of a recession.

As Milei’s support slips in the polls, investors wary of a country infamous for defaulting on its debt nine times are weighing the possibility that the Peronists — the populist movement that has long dominated Argentine politics — could return to power and reverse his market-friendly reforms. The premium investors demand to hold Argentina’s bonds, a gauge of perceived default risk, has more than doubled since early August, according to JPMorgan.

Under growing pressure, Milei is now hoping to overhaul next year’s presidential race. The Senate on Thursday approved his bill to suspend the mandatory primaries, which the government argues waste public money on contests parties should run themselves. It now goes to the lower house for a vote.

Suspending the primaries, long a bellwether for the general election, would spare Milei an early verdict from voters — one that, if poor, could spook markets and sink the peso and his support with it.
Peronist leaders have balked at the move, which would force their fractured movement to negotiate a ticket behind closed doors or scramble to organize a primary of its own.
"Milei now wants to change the rules of democracy to improve his chances of reelection by cheating,” Buenos Aires province Gov. Axel Kicillof, a potential Peronist challenger to Milei, wrote on X.

title: Hank Brown rushes for three touchdowns, throws for another in No. 13 Iowa's 31-7 win over Nebraska
summary: Iowa quarterback Hank Brown ran for three touchdowns and threw for another, and the No. 13 Hawkeyes defeated Nebraska 31-7
story: Iowa quarterback Hank Brown ran for three touchdowns and threw for another, and the No. 13 Hawkeyes defeated Nebraska 31-7
IOWA CITY, Iowa -- Iowa quarterback Hank Brown ran for three touchdowns and threw for another, and the No. 13 Hawkeyes defeated Nebraska 31-7 on Friday.

The Hawkeyes (10-2, 7-2 Big Ten) kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive and stayed in the race for a spot in the Big Ten championship game by winning their fifth consecutive game. Iowa has outscored its opponents 147-41, with its defense allowing only five touchdowns, in the winning streak.

Brown, who rushed for 48 yards and threw for 173, opened the scoring with a 14-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. His 6-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter gave Iowa a 17-7 lead, and his 29-yard run with 4:02 left in the game closed the scoring.
Brown’s 9-yard touchdown pass to tight end DJ Vonnahme put Iowa up 24-7 early in the fourth quarter.
Iowa, which has won 11 of the last 12 games against the Huskers, had a 329-260 advantage in offensive yards, the first time a team has outgained Nebraska (7-5, 4-5) this season.
Jamal Rule rushed for 106 yards and had a 21-yard touchdown run for the Huskers in the second quarter.

Nebraska: The Huskers, coming off last Saturday’s 31-28 win over Ohio State, had their chances in this game. They recovered a muffed punt midway through the third quarter, trailing 10-7, but were stopped on downs at the Iowa 35-yard line. They then gave up Brown’s second touchdown run on the ensuing possession.

Iowa: There are still combinations that have to happen for the Hawkeyes to make it to the Big Ten championship game, but they still have postseason hopes on not just the conference level but the national one. Iowa, which leads the nation in scoring defense, shut out its opponent in the second half for the third consecutive game.
Nebraska: TBD.
Iowa: TBD.

title: Jayden Reid scores 24 and hits 2 late free throws to help No. 24 Memphis hold off Wake Forest 88-85
summary: Jayden Reid scored 24 points and his two free throws with 5 seconds left helped No. 24 Memphis hold off Wake Forest 88-85 on Friday in the Championship Series at the Battle 4 Atlantis
story: Jayden Reid scored 24 points and his two free throws with 5 seconds left helped No. 24 Memphis hold off Wake Forest 88-85 on Friday in the Championship Series at the Battle 4 Atlantis

NASSAU, Bahamas -- Jayden Reid scored 24 points and his two free throws with 5 seconds left helped No. 24 Memphis hold off Wake Forest 88-85 on Friday in the Championship Series at the Battle 4 Atlantis.
Luke Almodovar had 20 points and Tylik Weeks added 11 for the Tigers (6-1).
Kevair Kennedy scored 29 points and made 13 of 13 free throws for the Demon Deacons (6-2). Justin Ray scored 13 and Isaac Carr, Gavin Placide and Jamari McDowell all scored 11.
Memphis led 65-45 with 10 minutes left before Wake Forest rallied. A layup by Kennedy got the Demon Deacons within 75-66 with 3 1/2 minutes to go.
Wake Forest kept chipping away at the Tigers' lead and 3-pointers by Ray and Carr along with a three-point play by Kennedy cut Memphis' lead to 84-80 with 30 seconds remaining.

Memphis led 86-82 with 16 seconds left when Weeks missed two free throws. Kennedy then drew a foul on Weeks while burying a jumper and converted the free throw. With Memphis leading 86-85, Reid was fouled and his two free throws provided the final margin. Almodovar's steal with 3 seconds left wrapped it up for Memphis.
Wake Forest led 17-15 nine minutes in before Memphis scored 16 of the next 19 points to lead 31-20 with about four minutes remaining in the half. Almodovar scored seven points in the run.
Memphis led 37-26 at halftime.
Memphis: The Tigers play Dayton at Columbus, Ohio, on Sunday.
Wake Forest: The Demon Deacons play at LSU on Tuesday.

title: Chargers QB Justin Herbert ruled out with concussion. DJ Uiagalelei will make first NFL start
summary: Justin Herbert will not clear the concussion protocol in time to play for the Chargers on Sunday, positioning DJ Uiagalelei to make his first career start when Los Angeles hosts the New England Patriots
story: Justin Herbert will not clear the concussion protocol in time to play for the Chargers on Sunday, positioning DJ Uiagalelei to make his first career start when Los Angeles hosts the New England Patriots

EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Justin Herbert will not clear the concussion protocol in time to play for the Chargers on Sunday, positioning DJ Uiagalelei to make his first career start when Los Angeles hosts the New England Patriots.
Herbert reported symptoms following a 27-24 loss to the New York Jets on Sunday, which dropped the Chargers to 1-9. He did not practice all week and was ruled out on Friday.

It was a dismal season for Herbert before the injury. He has completed 62.4% of his passes for 1,851 yards and eight touchdowns with 11 interceptions while struggling to adapt to new coordinator Mike McDaniel’s offense. Herbert has taken a league-high 39 sacks, including six against the Jets.

Uiagalelei is in his second NFL season, having made his debut in a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans on Nov. 8. He completed 2 of 7 throws for 24 yards and a touchdown after replacing Herbert in the fourth quarter.

A five-star recruit from Riverside, California, Uiagalelei never quite lived up to those evaluations during his two seasons as a starter at Clemson, where he succeeded Trevor Lawrence. Uiagalelei transferred to Oregon State in 2023 before heading to Florida State the next year to wrap up his college career.

Uiagalelei joined the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He had been on the practice squad before being signed to the active roster in late September. Uiagalelei became Herbert’s backup in October after Trey Lance went on injured reserve because of a groin injury.

Uiagalelei will be facing off against another backup, with the Patriots (5-5) starting Tommy DeVito after Drake Maye fractured his fibula in New England's loss to Detroit on Nov. 15 before a bye week.

To fill out their depth chart at quarterback, the Chargers signed Jake Browning to the active roster from the practice squad on Thursday. Cornerback Deane Leonard (groin) was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move.
Browning is a four-year NFL veteran who made 10 starts with the Cincinnati Bengals as Joe Burrow’s backup.

title: Jake West scores 23 points, Northwestern rallies to beat Northeastern 65-61
summary: Northwestern rallies from a 10-point deficit to beat Northeastern 65-61 on Friday night
story: Northwestern rallies from a 10-point deficit to beat Northeastern 65-61 on Friday night
EVANSTON, Ill. -- Jake West scored 18 of his 23 points in the second half and Northwestern rallied from a 10-point deficit to beat Northeastern 65-61 on Friday night.
Northeastern used a 12-2 run to take a 51-41 lead with about eight minutes remaining. Northwestern answered with a 14-4 surge to tie it 55-all with 3:55 to play.

An Angelo Ciaravino dunk followed by a LA Pratt jumper gave Northwestern a 62-59 lead with 50 seconds left. The teams traded free throws before Louis Bond missed a 3-pointer for Northeastern with nine seconds to go and Pratt added a free throw to seal it.
West shot 6 of 17 from the floor and made all 10 of his free-throw attempts. Okku Federiko, a reserve, added 13 points and 12 rebounds for Northwestern (5-3). Ciaravino finished with 10 points.
Rashad King had 23 points and Bond scored 15 for Northeastern (2-6). Dorian Grosber added 10 points and 10 rebounds.
The game was tied 30-all at halftime. King and Bond each scored 10 points before the break. Northwestern's Jack Karasinski scored all nine of his points in the first half to pace the Wildcats.
Northeastern: hosts Holy Cross on Wednesday.
Northwestern: at home against Wisconsin on Tuesday.

title: Isaiah Joe scores 22 points, Pistons' reserves power NBA Cup win over Bucks
summary: Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night
story: Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night
DETROIT -- Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night.

The Pistons wpn East Group A at 3-1 with a better points differential than the Toronto Raptors and Orlando Magic. Detroit will host a knockout-round game and could finish with the Eastern Conference's top seed.
The Bucks finished 0-4 in group play.

The Pistons, who finished with seven players in double figures, were missing three starters — Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) have been out for weeks, and Cade Cunningham (knee) also was in street clothes.
Paul Reed and fellow reserve Elijah Harkless added 14 points. Detroit had 60 bench points while the starters finished with 53.
Rookie Brayden Burries had 23 points for the Bucks and Tyler Herro added 20.

Milwaukee led by 16 points in the first quarter, but only had a two-point advantage at halftime. The Pistons then put up a 42-point third quarter that included points from eight players. Daniss Jenkins' 3-pointer at the buzzer put Detroit up 90-78 at quarter's end.
Officials and coaches had to jump in between the players midway through the fourth after Myles Turner fired a ball into Ausar Thompson's back. Both players were given technical fouls.
After the confrontation, the game turned into a dunk fest for the Pistons, who got points from nine players in an 64-point second half.

The Bucks had a rare good start, taking a 19-3 lead before Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff pulled all of his starters. The reserves got Detroit back into the game, then went on a 15-2 run to take the lead in the second quarter.
Milwaukee led 50-48 at halftime, with Detroit's starters only contributing 12 points.

title: Italy advances to the Davis Cup final with win over Czech Republic

Musetti and Vavassori went ‌a set down against Jiri Lehecka and Tomas Machac. But encouraged by a partisan crowd, they came back for ‌a 3-6, 6-1, 7-6 (4) win in Bologna.

Musetti, who returned to Davis ​Cup action for the first time since 2024 this ‌week, had put Italy ahead with a 6-3, 6-4 win over Jakub Mensik in the opening singles. But Lehecka leveled the match for the Czechs when he beat world No. 7 Flavio Cobolli 6-2, 1-6, 6-3.

title: Dante Allen scores 23 as No. 17 Miami beats No. 15 Alabama in the first of back-to-back matchups
summary: Dante Allen scored 23 points to lead No. 17 Miami past No. 15 Alabama, 87-81, in the fifth-place game of the Players Era 16 tournament Friday night
story: Dante Allen scored 23 points to lead No. 17 Miami past No. 15 Alabama, 87-81, in the fifth-place game of the Players Era 16 tournament Friday night
LAS VEGAS -- Dante Allen scored 23 points to lead No. 17 Miami past No. 15 Alabama, 87-81, in the fifth-place game of the Players Era 16 tournament Friday night.
The Hurricanes and Crimson Tide will meet again on Wednesday night in a scheduled SEC/ACC Challenge matchup in Coral Gables, Florida.
Malik Reneau added 14 points and four steals for the Hurricanes (7-2), while Shelton Henderson had 13 points and five assists and Acaden Lewis scored 10. Robert Miller III grabbed 10 rebounds.

Brandon Garrison led Alabama (6-2) with 20 points despite missing the final 6:23 after being helped off the court with an ankle injury. Aden Holloway added 18 points and six assists, while Drew Fielder and Qayden Samuels each scored 11 points.
Alabama trailed 74-63 with 8:38 remaining but scored nine consecutive points, including a 3-pointer by Holloway, to cut the deficit to 74-72 with 6:08 left.
Miami extended its lead back to five on a free throw by Allen and a basket by Lewis. Alabama wouldn’t get closer than four points the rest of the way.

Miami got off to a fast start. After a layup by Garrison, the Hurricanes scored 11 consecutive points to take an 11-2 lead with 15:27 remaining in the first half. Allen scored seven points during the run.

Alabama cut the deficit to 13-10, but Miami responded with a 12-2 run to build its largest lead of the half, 25-12. Alabama eventually trimmed the deficit to two points, 40-38, with 3:31 remaining in the half.
The Hurricanes closed the half with a 12-2 run to take a 52-40 lead into the break. Lewis had a fast-break layup and made two free throws in the final 1:02.

title: NBA Cup quarterfinals set: Celtics-Pistons, 76ers-Hawks, Spurs-Mavericks, Grizzlies-Trail Blazers
summary: Philadelphia’s LeBron James and San Antonio’s Victor Wembanyama are headed back to the NBA Cup quarterfinals
story: Philadelphia’s LeBron James and San Antonio’s Victor Wembanyama are headed back to the NBA Cup quarterfinals

Philadelphia's LeBron James and San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama are headed back to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. So is Dallas' Cooper Flagg, along with some teams that are about to experience the knockout round for the first time.
Oh, and there will be a new champion as well.

The NBA Cup quarterfinals are now set. Detroit, Atlanta, Philadelphia and Boston are on the Eastern Conference side of the bracket, while Dallas, Portland, Memphis and San Antonio — last year's runner-up — are headed there from the Western Conference.
“We’re in it,” James said. “Everyone knows about the Cup games, and everyone knows the importance of it and trying to play for something.”

Detroit, Philadelphia and Memphis are in the knockout round for the first time. Dallas is the only team that went unbeaten in group play, going 4-0 in West Group A — and erasing a 21-point deficit against Phoenix on Friday night to seal up the No. 1 seed.

“The Cup is fun," Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg said on the team broadcast after a 34-point, seven-rebound, eight-assist, five-steal, four-block masterpiece. "It adds a whole new element to the season. It's been a blast to be able to play in it and compete. To lock down the No. 1 seed is pretty big."

The Hawks are headed to the tournament quarterfinals by the slimmest of margins. Atlanta (3-1 in Cup play) won East Group C by beating Boston 87-86 on Friday. If the Hawks had lost, they would have been eliminated.

“I think this was a gritty, gritty win,” Hawks coach Quin Snyder said. “For us to be rewarded for playing that way, I think it’s something we can hang on to. This is a unique format, this tournament ... but if we can compete like that, we always have a chance.”

Boston (3-1) ended up as the East’s wild-card team because it outscored teams by 67 points in group play — well ahead of the East’s other wild-card contenders that finished at 3-1, those being Toronto (+34), Miami (+28) and Orlando (-1).
Detroit clinched East Group A with a 113-98 win over Milwaukee. The Pistons moved into the knockout stage for the first time.

“It’s something we haven’t done before,” Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. “To be able to get an opportunity with this group, to continue to do things that we haven’t done in the past, it’s great for us.”

San Antonio rallied from 20 down to beat the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 and advance to the quarterfinals as the West's wild card team. Stephon Castle had 26 points and Wembanyama finished with 25 for the Spurs.
“We're battle tested,” Castle said.

Memphis beat Minnesota in a winner-take-all game to decide West Group B, and Portland's win over Golden State helped seal West Group C for the Trail Blazers. It means Ja Morant's old team in Memphis will play Ja Morant's new team in Portland for a spot in the Cup semifinals.
“Any time you are playing for anything of value ... it's always good," Blazers coach Micah Nori said. “And it's good to win.”
James and the 76ers clinched their spot with a 111-87 win over Indiana. James was the tournament's first MVP when he led the Los Angeles Lakers to the inaugural title in 2023.
“I've been part of it before,” James said. "Just trying to seize the opportunity now that it's here.”
East quarterfinals
— No. 3 Philadelphia at No. 2 Atlanta, Dec. 4, 7 p.m. EST.
— No. 4 Boston at No. 1 Detroit, Dec. 5, 7:30 p.m. EST.
West quarterfinals
— No. 4 San Antonio at No. 1 Dallas, Dec. 4, 9:30 p.m. EST.
— No. 3 Memphis at No. 2 Portland, Dec. 5, 10 p.m. EST.

There is a trophy and medals for the winner — the final is Dec. 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, the home arena for Butler University — as well as money, and the quarterfinalists have already earned a bonus.
— Players on teams that lose in the quarterfinals get $60,499.
— Players on teams that lose in the semifinals get $120,997.
— Players on the runner-up team get $241,994.
— Players on the NBA Cup championship team get $604,985.
Those on two-way contracts will get half those amounts.
East Group A: Detroit 3-1, Toronto 3-1, Orlando 3-1, Brooklyn 1-3, Milwaukee 0-4.
— Pistons advanced on point-differential tiebreaker.
East Group B: Philadelphia 3-1, Miami 3-1, Cleveland 2-2, Indiana 1-3, New York 1-3.
— 76ers advanced on head-to-head tiebreaker with Heat.
East Group C: Atlanta 3-1, Boston 3-1, Washington 2-2, Chicago 2-2, Charlotte 0-4.
— Hawks advanced on head-to-head tiebreaker with Celtics, who claimed wild-card over Raptors, Magic and Heat on point differential.
West Group A: Dallas 4-0, Denver 3-1, Houston 2-2, Phoenix 1-3, Utah 0-4.
— Mavs only unbeaten team in group play this season.
West Group B: Memphis 3-1, Minnesota 3-1, Oklahoma City 2-2, New Orleans 1-3, LA Clippers 1-3.
— Grizzlies advanced on head-to-head tiebreaker with Timberwolves.
West Group C: Portland 3-1, San Antonio 3-1, Golden State 2-2, LA Lakers 2-2, Sacramento 0-4.
— Blazers had head-to-head on Spurs for group, Spurs topped Nuggets and Wolves in point differential for wild card.
No team has ever gone back-to-back as Cup champions and that won't change until at least 2027.
The New York Knicks — who beat San Antonio for the Cup title last year and beat the Spurs again in the NBA Finals — were eliminated Friday night by losing to Miami 108-105.

The Knicks finished group play at 1-3; there were some scenarios entering the night where they could have advanced by finishing 2-2, but ultimately the other results Friday meant the Knicks wouldn't have moved on even with a win.

title: Jamal Murray scores 36 to lead Nuggets past Jazz 120-107
summary: Jamal Murray scored 36 points to rally the Denver Nuggets to a 120-107 victory over the Utah Jazz in NBA Cup group play on Friday night
story: Jamal Murray scored 36 points to rally the Denver Nuggets to a 120-107 victory over the Utah Jazz in NBA Cup group play on Friday night
SALT LAKE CITY -- Jamal Murray scored 36 points to rally the Denver Nuggets to a 120-107 victory over the Utah Jazz in NBA Cup group play on Friday night.
Nikola Jokic tallied 17 points, 15 assists, and nine rebounds for the Nuggets. Christian Braun added 20 points and eight rebounds.
Keyonte George scored 25 points and Darryn Peterson added 20 to lead the Jazz. Svi Mykhailiuk added 18 points off the bench.

Jusuf Nurkic made his season debut after missing Utah’s first 19 games with a toe injury and finished with a team-high 11 assists. Nurkic’s crisp passing helped elevate the Jazz offense following a sluggish start.
Utah seized a 102-97 lead after Ace Bailey threw down an alley oop dunk to punctuate a string of three straight baskets for the Jazz.

Denver erased the deficit behind an 11-0 run, taking a 108-104 lead with 3:25 left on Murray’s step-back 3-pointer that capped the run. Mykhailiuk cut it back to one on a 3, but Utah drew no closer after the Nuggets scored on five straight possessions, punctuated by Murray’s finger roll layup and free throw.
Denver staked out a 24-10 lead deep into the first quarter behind a hot start from Jokic. He scored three baskets and assisted on three others to help the Nuggets take control early.
Utah chipped away at the deficit and finally took their first lead at 31-29 early in the second quarter when Brice Sensabaugh capped a 9-2 run with a 3-pointer.
The Jazz traded baskets with the Nuggets and led through most of the third quarter, going up by as many as six points when Mykhailiuk drove for a layup to put Utah up 81-75.

Jazz: Host Phoenix on Sunday.

title: Spurs ride second-half surge to earn spot in NBA Cup knockout round with 99-96 victory over Lakers
summary: Stephon Castle scored 26 points as the San Antonio Spurs secured a 99-96 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers to advance to the NBA Cup knockout round
story: Stephon Castle scored 26 points as the San Antonio Spurs secured a 99-96 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers to advance to the NBA Cup knockout round

SAN ANTONIO -- Stephon Castle had 26 points, Victor Wembanyama had 25 points and 16 rebounds, and the San Antonio Spurs surged in the second half for a 99-96 win over the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup knockout round.
Castle was 10 for 15 from the field, including a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 96-90 with 43.4 seconds remaining following De’Aaron Fox’s rebound of Wembanyama’s missed free throw.
Luka Doncic had 31 points to lead Los Angeles, which was eliminated from the NBA Cup with the loss. Austin Reaves added 21 points and Walker Kessler had 10 points and 13 rebounds.

Reaves was 5 for 9 on 3-pointers, including a 25-footer with 34 seconds remaining that cut the Spurs’ lead to 96-93. Jake LaRavia hit a pair of free throws after Fox lost possession on a double dribble. Fox responded with a pair of free throws with 6.6 seconds left that put the Spurs up 98-95.
San Antonio overcame an anemic first half, outscoring Los Angeles 30-14 in the third quarter with Keldon Johnson’s 3-pointer with two seconds remaining tying the game at 68 entering the fourth.

The Lakers took a 27-14 lead in the opening period as the Spurs shot 7 for 18 in posting a season-low for points in any quarter this season. San Antonio also set a season-low for any half in trailing 54-38 at halftime.

Castle hit consecutive 3-pointers to put San Antonio ahead 81-73 with his second 3 coming after Carter Bryant went soaring through the lane for an offensive rebound. Bryant finished with three points, three rebounds and several key defensive plays during the Spurs' rally.
San Antonio lost to the New York Knicks in last season’s NBA Cup final.

title: Jerry Jones says he still believes in Brian Schottenheimer despite mounting meltdowns by Cowboys
summary: Jerry Jones says he still believes Brian Schottenheimer is the right coach for the Dallas Cowboys
story: Jerry Jones says he still believes Brian Schottenheimer is the right coach for the Dallas Cowboys
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Jerry Jones says he still believes Brian Schottenheimer is the right coach for the Dallas Cowboys.
There was a significant qualifier from the owner and general manager after yet another meltdown in a 39-38 loss to Philadelphia on Thanksgiving.
“I do,” Jones said when asked if he still believed his second-year coach could lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl. “I do, but on the other hand, these are setbacks and they’re damning setbacks.”

Fans surely will see the most damning of all as Schottenheimer's decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with a two-point lead and 55 seconds remaining. Dak Prescott was sacked for a 9-yard loss, leaving the Eagles just 11 yards from the spot for Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds remaining.

Jones didn't want to pin the latest loss on that decision either, even though Ty Robinson, the defensive lineman who sacked Prescott, was surprised Dallas snapped the ball. And WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark seemed similarly puzzled.
“I’m not going to take any one thing because one thing shouldn’t have done it,” Jones said. “We really had a combination of things that we miscued on.”
The Cowboys (5-7) will have to sit on a stunning loss for 11 days before they return for a Monday night game at Seattle on Dec. 7.
Playoff hopes aren't realistic at the moment. Here are some of the realities for Dallas:

— No other home team in NFL history has lost four home games in the same season when scoring at least 30 points, or averaged at least 30 points in the first 12 games (31.3) of a season and had a losing record.
— The largest blown fourth-quarter lead in franchise history was 14 points. The Cowboys matched that twice in November — both at home.

— Schottenheimer botched the final seconds of a 34-31 loss to Baltimore in Rio de Janeiro and has his latest baffling decision to go with it. Those aren't the only two questionable moments with game management.
— Regardless of how they're happening, the losses are mounting. Dallas is 12-16-1 and has spent just one week over .500 under Schottenheimer (6-5-1 last season).
The coach insists he isn't listening to the noise about his job security.
“I don’t worry about that,” Schottenheimer said. “I worry about the guys in that locker room, and it doesn’t affect me.”

The Cowboys have already made the midseason hire of Mike Pettine as a senior assistant for first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dallas subsequently stripped play-calling duties from the 34-year-old Parker and gave them to Pettine, who turned 60 a few weeks before deciding to come out of retirement.
Jones had already said no more coaching changes were coming. He said it again going into a long weekend and a 10-day gap between games.
“I wouldn’t anticipate that,” Jones said. “We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive in my mind without coaching changes at this time.”

Prescott has accounted for 20 touchdowns (17 passing, three rushing) with two interceptions — one of them meaningless on the final play against the Eagles — in the past six games. The Cowboys are 3-3.

Yes, the Dallas defense is bad. The Cowboys have given up at least one touchdown of 50 or more yards in five consecutive games. Breakdowns on special teams have been crippling, too. The first time it felt like Dallas was in trouble against Philadelphia was when the Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown. Then right after the Cowboys restored a 14-point lead, they gave up a 55-yard kickoff return.

WR KaVontae Turpin probably deserves some credit for an offense that scored on 12 of 13 drives with 11 touchdowns over six quarters from the start of a 51-30 victory over Tennessee to halftime against Philadelphia. Turpin had a 22-yard scoring run against the Titans and a 31-yard TD catch on a screen against the Eagles. His return from a rib injury has made an already potent offense seem more explosive.

The Cowboys have let three backup quarterbacks beat them at home this season. Undrafted Tampa Bay rookie Jalon Daniels had a 110.2 passer rating against Dallas compared to an average of 57.0 in his other two starts. Arizona's Gardner Minshew had a 137.3 rating after replacing an ineffective Jacoby Brissett, then an 83.5 rating in his only start the next week, when he tore a ligament in his elbow. Milton was at 121.8 against the Cowboys after the ratings in his first two career starts for the Eagles were 66.9 and 73.7.
Schottenheimer said DT Quinnen Williams had back spasms. ... CB Joey Porter Jr. exited in the first half appearing to favor his right arm or shoulder but returned to the game on the same series.

129 — The point total for the Cowboys over a three-game span, three shy of the franchise record from 1968 when Dallas won all three at the start of a 12-2 regular season. These Cowboys went 1-2 in those games.

Even if they win three of the next four games against playoff-caliber opponents, the Cowboys would be 8-8 going into the finale. The NFC East-leading New York Giants would have to go 2-4 in their next six for Dallas to have a chance to catch them.

title: Wisconsin trounces Minnesota 28-5 to regain possession of Paul Bunyan's Axe
summary: Colton Joseph threw a touchdown pass and ran for two more scores while Wisconsin’s defense continued its season-long home dominance in the Badgers’ 28-5 victory over Minnesota on Friday night
story: Colton Joseph threw a touchdown pass and ran for two more scores while Wisconsin’s defense continued its season-long home dominance in the Badgers’ 28-5 victory over Minnesota on Friday night

MADISON, Wis. -- Colton Joseph threw a touchdown pass and ran for two more scores while Wisconsin’s defense continued its season-long home dominance in the Badgers’ 28-5 victory over Minnesota on Friday night.

Wisconsin (8-4, 6-3 Big Ten) outgained Minnesota 482-115 and beat the Gophers for just the second time in six years to regain possession of Paul Bunyan’s Axe, the prize that goes to the winner of this annual matchup. It also enabled Wisconsin to tie the most-played series of any Bowl Subdivision rivalry at 64-64-8.

The blowout victory capped a regular season in which Wisconsin doubled its win total from last year. The domination of a rival also represented a step forward for Badgers coach Luke Fickell, whose future at Wisconsin has been the subject of speculation throughout the season in part because of his struggles in rivalry games.
Wisconsin has gone 0-4 against Iowa during Fickell’s tenure and had been 1-2 against Minnesota (6-6, 4-5) before Friday.

Joseph rushed for 101 yards on 20 carries and completed 12 of 18 passes for 217 yards, including a 27-yard touchdown to Tyrell Henry. He had touchdown runs of 7 yards in the second quarter and 1 yard in the third period.
He also threw two interceptions, though the second one came after the ball bounced off the hands of Wisconsin receiver Eugene Hilton Jr.
Joseph has rushed for 659 yards this year to set a single-season record for a Wisconsin quarterback. Tanner McAvoy had the previous record after rushing for 574 yards in 2014.

Wisconsin allowed only 44 points in six home games this season and didn't give up more than 10 points in any of them. The last time Wisconsin went a full season without yielding more than 10 points in any home game was in 1951.
Two of Minnesota’s points Friday came on a safety after Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins committed a holding penalty in the end zone.

The Badgers led 21-3 after a first half in which they controlled possession for 22 1/2 minutes and outgained Minnesota 298-39. During that first half, Wisconsin produced 16 first downs and Minnesota had just one.
Minnesota took an early 3-0 lead on Lucas Drzewiecki’s 53-yard field goal after Naiim Parrish had an 18-yard interception return off a Joseph pass on the game’s opening series.
But the Badgers dominated from there. Wisconsin scored touchdowns on each of its next three drivers while forcing three straight Minnesota three-and-outs.
Wisconsin pulled ahead for good on the opening play of the second quarter when Joseph connected with Henry on a third-and-13 play.
Henry celebrated the touchdown by sitting down and pretending he was rowing a boat, an apparent mockery of the “row the boat” slogan frequently used by Minnesota coach P.J. Fleck.
The night only got rougher for Fleck and the Gophers the rest of the way.

Minnesota: Considering the team with the highest rushing total has now won 20 of the last 21 Wisconsin-Minnesota matchups, the Gophers never gave themselves a chance by getting outrushed 265-11 on Friday. The Gophers also lost defensive end Jaxon Howard and nickel back Aidan Gousby to injuries in the first half.

Wisconsin: Joseph continued his remarkable late-season surge. The Old Dominion transfer had thrown for fewer than 100 yards in three straight games before freshman Ryan Hopkins took over as Wisconsin's starting quarterback in early November. Joseph regained the starting spot last week at Purdue and has totaled 414 yards passing and 215 yards rushing in two lopsided victories.
Both teams wait to learn their bowl destinations.

title: Sanchez hat trick sends USWNT to the World Cup with 8-0 qualifying victory over El Salvador
summary: Ashley Sanchez scored three goals in the first half and the United States secured a spot in the 2027 Women’s World Cup with an 8-0 victory over El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Championship
story: Ashley Sanchez scored three goals in the first half and the United States secured a spot in the 2027 Women’s World Cup with an 8-0 victory over El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Championship

MANSFIELD, Texas -- Ashley Sanchez scored three goals in the first half and the United States secured a spot in the 2027 Women's World Cup with an 8-0 victory over El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Championship on Friday night.
The United States advances to the semifinals to play Jamaica, which clinched a World Cup berth earlier in the day with a 3-0 quarterfinal victory over Costa Rica at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium.

The quarterfinals continue on Saturday with Canada facing Panama and Mexico meeting Haiti. All four quarterfinal winners earn direct berths in the World Cup in Brazil. The remaining teams will play for the confederation’s two spots in the intercontinental playoffs.

The United States, currently ranked No. 2 in the world, has won four World Cups, most recently in 2019. The team had a disappointing finish in the 2023 tournament when they were eliminated in the round of 16 by Sweden. El Salvador, ranked No. 78, has never played in a World Cup.

The U.S. squad, the defending W Championship winners, were without Trinity Rodman, who was injured in the National Women’s Soccer League championship game. While the team characterized it as a minor shoulder injury, Rodman was replaced on the 23-player roster for the tournament by Jaedyn Shaw.

Mallory Swanson, Sophia Wilson and Alyssa Thompson made up the U.S. front line against El Salvador. Coach Emma Hayes, who has rotated goalkeepers since the retirement of Alyssa Naeher, started Claudia Dickey.

The U.S. team scored seven goals in the first half. Defender Kennedy Wesley scored the opening goal for the United States in the ninth minute, taking cross from Wilson while rushing forward and directing the ball into the net.

Another defender, Tierna Davidson, scored on a header off Swanson's free kick in the 31st minute. Just moments later, Wilson sent the ball up to Swanson, who scored from the middle of the box. It was Swanson's 40th goal for the national team.
Sanchez, the NWSL Golden Boot winner with 20 goals for the North Carolina Courage this season, made it 4-0 with a goal in the 36th and another from distance into the top corner in the 39th.
Sanchez added a third goal in the 43rd minute before Wilson made it 7-0 before halftime with a goal in the 45th.
Croix Bethune, the NWSL's midfielder of the year, added a goal in the 80th minute off a feed from Lindsey Horan.
After El Salvador lost back-to-back matches to Paraguay in the October window, coach Eric Acuna sparked controversy when he publicly disparaged his team and called out individual players.
His comments were condemned by the nation’s soccer federation, which said any statement that “discredits, belittles or publicly exposes in a derogatory manner” is unacceptable.
The United States played world No. 1 Spain in the October window, falling 2-0 in the opening match before a 2-2 draw in the second.

title: Penguins snap a 5-game skid with a 6-3 victory over the Sabres
summary: Ben Kindel, Rutger McGroarty, Ville Koivunen and Evgeni Malkin each had a goal and an assist, and the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Buffalo Sabres 6-3 on Friday night to snap a five-game losing streak
story: Ben Kindel, Rutger McGroarty, Ville Koivunen and Evgeni Malkin each had a goal and an assist, and the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Buffalo Sabres 6-3 on Friday night to snap a five-game losing streak

BUFFALO, N.Y. -- Ben Kindel, Rutger McGroarty, Ville Koivunen and Evgeni Malkin each had a goal and an assist, and the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Buffalo Sabres 6-3 on Friday night to snap a five-game losing streak.
Kris Letang and Blake Letang also scored for the Penguins. Sergei Murashov made 20 saves for Pittsburgh, the last-place team in the Eastern Conference.

Kindel, McGroarty and Koivunen became the first trio of Pittsburgh players age 23 or younger to record multiple goals in the same game since Sidney Crosby, Jordan Staal and Letang accomplished the feat on March 6, 2010.
Rasmus Dahlin had a goal and an assist for the Sabres, who were coming off a 5-1 win against the New York Rangers, their third in four games. Jiri Kulich and Josh Norris also scored.
Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed four goals on 10 shots before getting replaced three minutes into the second period. Alex Lyon stopped 17 of the 18 shots he faced.
The Penguins scored twice early in the second period after the teams traded goals throughout the first.

McGroarty deflected Koivunen’s shot past Luukkonen for his first goal of the season 30 seconds into the second, and Lizotte scored his first from the high slot at 3:15 of the period. Koivunen made it 5-3 with 1:16 remaining in the second.
Malkin got his eighth of the season into the empty net with 2:01 to go in the third.

Kulich gave Buffalo the lead 31 seconds into the game when he finished a 2-on-1 with Dahlin, extending his scoring streak to four games and recording his seventh point in six games. Dahlin’s goal on a power play midway through the period gave the Sabres a 2-1 lead
Kindel batted in a bouncing puck near the net for an unassisted goal at 7:42 into the first, and Kindel assisted on Letang’s tying goal with 40 seconds left in the opening period.
Penguins: Conclude back-to-back hosting Toronto on Saturday night.
Sabres: Open four-game trip at Edmonton on Tuesday night.

title: Vokietaitis has 29 points, 11 rebounds as No. 7 Texas beats Saint Mary's 76-73 to win Rady title
summary: Matas Vokietaitis had 29 points and 11 rebounds for No. 7 Texas, which used a late 13-0 run to overtake Saint Mary’s and win 76-73 in the Rady Children’s Invitational championship game
story: Matas Vokietaitis had 29 points and 11 rebounds for No. 7 Texas, which used a late 13-0 run to overtake Saint Mary’s and win 76-73 in the Rady Children’s Invitational championship game

SAN DIEGO -- Matas Vokietaitis had 29 points and 11 rebounds as No. 7 Texas used a late 13-0 run to overtake Saint Mary's for a 76-73 win in the Rady Children's Invitational championship game on Friday.
Isaiah Johnson added 21 points for the Longhorns (8-0), including nine in the 13-point run that carried them from a 55-48 deficit to a 61-55 lead with 3:31 to go.

The Gaels (7-2), under first-year coach Mickey McConnell, were trying to beat Top 10 opponents on consecutive days for the first time. They stunned No. 6 UCLA 85-70 on Thursday, hitting 15 of 28 3-point shots to beat the highest-ranked nonconference team in program history.

The Gaels went up 55-48 on a floater by Vangelis Zougris with 6:46 left before the Longhorns started their run. Johnson had two layups and a 3-pointer to tie it at 55 before Elyjah Freeman had a steal and a dunk to give the Longhorns the lead for good at 57-55. Vokietaitis made two free throws and Johnson made a layup to make it 61-55.
The Gaels pulled within 74-71 on a layup by Joshua Dent with six seconds before Vokietaitis made two free throws with 5.7 seconds left. Dent hit a jumper at the buzzer.
Vokietaitis bounced back after fouling out midway through the second half of Thursday’s 92-83 win against Georgetown. He had only five points and one rebound in 13 minutes against the Hoyas.
Freeman had 12 points and David Punch 10 for Texas.

Zougris scored 15 of his 19 points in the first half. He was whistled for two quick fouls in the first 1 1/2 minutes of the second half, giving him four and forcing McConnell to sub him out with the Gaels leading 37-29.
He came back in with 12:41 to go just before Vokietaitis made two free throws to make it 45-42, the closest it had been since the first half.
Jeremy Dent-Smith had 15 points and Darius Bivins 12 for Saint Mary's.
McConnell was promoted after Randy Bennett left for Arizona State after 25 seasons with the Gaels. McConnell played under Bennett from 2007-11.
Texas plays at Louisville on Tuesday night in the SEC/ACC Challenge.
Saint Mary's hosts Hofstra on Tuesday night.

title: Trio rallies Texas A&M to 76-74 victory over Marquette at Battle 4 Atlantis
summary: PJ Haggerty and Mackenzie Mgbako both scored 21 points, and Jordan Pope picked up a loose ball and scored at the buzzer to lift Texas A&M to a 76-74 victory over Marquette in the Signature Series of the Battle 4 Atlantis
story: PJ Haggerty and Mackenzie Mgbako both scored 21 points, and Jordan Pope picked up a loose ball and scored at the buzzer to lift Texas A&M to a 76-74 victory over Marquette in the Signature Series of the Battle 4 Atlantis

NASSAU, Bahamas -- PJ Haggerty and Mackenzie Mgbako both scored 21 points, and Jordan Pope picked up a loose ball and scored at the buzzer to lift Texas A&M to a 76-74 victory over Marquette on Friday in the Signature Series of the Battle 4 Atlantis.
Colin Porter buried a 3-pointer to tie it 74-all with 10 seconds to go before Pope won it after Porter knocked the ball loose from Haggerty.

Haggerty made 6 of 15 shots and 8 of 11 free throws for the Aggies (7-1), who bounced back from their first loss — an 88-83 setback to Xavier in the first round of the event. Mgbako made four 3-pointers and added six rebounds, three steals and two blocks.
Pope finished with 14 points and five assists, while Jalen Shelley scored 13 with four assists for Texas A&M.
Nigel James Jr. led the Golden Eagles (4-4) with 24 points and 11 assists. Porter scored 15 off the bench on 5-for-8 shooting from 3-point range. Royce Parham totaled 10 points and seven rebounds.
Marquette took a 40-37 lead into halftime, and James sank two free throws to put Marquette up 66-55 with 10:11 remaining.
The Aggies chipped away until Haggerty made four straight free throws for a 74-72 lead with 1:36 left.
Marquette: Hosts Wagner on Tuesday.
Texas A&M: Hosts Stanford on Wednesday.

title: Kakko scores twice in 3rd as Kraken hand Oilers their 5th straight loss
summary: Kaapo Kakko scored twice in a two-minute span in the third period and the Seattle Kraken beat Edmonton 4-2 on Friday night, handing the Oilers their fifth straight loss in the opener the home-and-home set
story: Kaapo Kakko scored twice in a two-minute span in the third period and the Seattle Kraken beat Edmonton 4-2 on Friday night, handing the Oilers their fifth straight loss in the opener the home-and-home set

EDMONTON, Alberta -- Kaapo Kakko scored twice in a two-minute span in the third period and the Seattle Kraken beat Edmonton 4-2 on Friday night, handing the Oilers their fifth straight loss in the opener the home-and-home set.
The teams will meet again Saturday night in Seattle.
Jordan Eberle and Vince Dunn also scored and Matty Beniers had two assists for the Kraken (12-10-1). They have won two of their last three and snapped an eight-game road skid against the Oilers.
Philipp Grubauer made 16 stops before suffering an upper-body injury and being replaced by Joey Daccord, who made nine saves.
Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl scored for the skidding Oilers (17-7-4). Edmonton went 1 for 8 on the power play.

McDavid extended his season-opening home points streak to 14 games and became the sixth player in NHL history to reach 60 points in 28 games or fewer — the first since Mario Lemieux did so in 1995-96 in 21 contests. The other ones to hit 60 this early were Wayne Gretzky, Bernie Nicholls, Mike Bossy and Phil Esposito.
Tristan Jarry made 27 saves for Edmonton.

title: Harrison scores 20 as Washington State downs Idaho 69-61
summary: Ronnie Harrison Jr. scores 20 points and grabs 13 rebounds as Washington State beats Idaho 69-61
story: Ronnie Harrison Jr. scores 20 points and grabs 13 rebounds as Washington State beats Idaho 69-61
PULLMAN, Wash. -- Ronnie Harrison Jr. scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds as Washington State beat Idaho 69-61 on Friday.
Lazerek Houston shot 3 of 7 from the field and 8 of 9 from the free-throw line to add 14 points for the Cougars (4-4).
Kase Wynott finished with 26 points for the Vandals (4-4). Idaho also got 11 points from Kristian Gonzalez. Seth Joba finished with five points, 10 rebounds and two blocks.

Washington State entered halftime up 32-28. Harrison paced the Cougars in the first half with seven points. Washington State took the lead for good with 4:53 remaining in the second half on a layup from Tyler Kropp to make it a 54-53 game.
Up next
Washington State next plays Monday against Murray State on the road, and Idaho will visit Northern Colorado on Thursday.

title: Trail Blazers beat the Warriors 116-94 to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals
summary: Deni Avdija had 26 points and eight rebounds, Toumani Camara added 20 points and eight rebounds and the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Golden State Warriors 116-94 on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals
story: Deni Avdija had 26 points and eight rebounds, Toumani Camara added 20 points and eight rebounds and the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Golden State Warriors 116-94 on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals

PORTLAND, Ore. -- Deni Avdija had 26 points and eight rebounds, Toumani Camara added 20 points and eight rebounds and the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Golden State Warriors 116-94 on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals.

Portland led by 36 points in the first half and Golden State cut it to 10 in the fourth quarter before Portland regained control. With its margin of victory and San Antonio’s win over the Lakers, Portland will host the Memphis Grizzlies on Dec. 5.
Scoot Henderson added 18 points for Portland off the bench.
Yaxel Lendeborg led the Warriors with 18 points. Golden State is playing without Stephen Curry as he recovers from a torn oblique muscle.
Portland jumped out to a 37-11 first quarter lead as the Warriors shot 4 for 24 from the field and committed six turnovers in the first quarter.
Portland started the second quarter with a 10-0 run and pushed their lead to 36 at 47-11. The Warriors mounted their comeback in stages, starting with a 13-2 run to cut the lead to 49-24.
Lendeborg cut the lead to 12 on a 3-pointer with 2:39 left in the third quarter at 88-76. The Warriors cut the lead to 10 one more time on a layup by Lendeborg with just over five minutes left.
Portland’s Damian Lillard did not play with right calf tightness, which coach Micah Nori said was a “day-to-day,” situation.
Warriors; Hosts the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday night.
Trail Blazers: Host New Orleans on Sunday.

title: B.J. Davis takes over in OT, Creighton beats No. 22 Gonzaga 97-89
summary: B
story: B
LAS VEGAS -- B.J. Davis scored 10 of his 27 points in overtime, including five free throws down the stretch, and Creighton beat No. 22 Gonzaga 97-89 on Friday night in a Players Era 16 bracket final.
The Bluejays will play No. 25 Louisville in the championship game on Saturday night. Louisville beat Tennessee 84-64.
Davis also had 11 rebounds and 11 assists. Wes Enis scored 28 points, and Austin Swartz added 11 for Creighton (7-1).
Chauncey Wiggins led Gonzaga (5-2) with 22 points, while Davis Fogle scored 21.

Davis drove for a layup to put Creighton ahead 86-83 with 1:58 remaining in overtime. After a Gonzaga miss, Fredrick King scored on a layup. Gonzaga then turned the ball over and Davis made a 3-pointer to give Creighton a 91-83 lead.
Fogle answered with a 3-pointer to pull Gonzaga within 91-86 with 33 seconds remaining.

Davis was fouled with 32.9 seconds left and made both free throws. Wiggins hit a deep 3-pointer with 26.4 seconds remaining to cut Creighton’s lead to 93-89. Enis made both free throws to extend the lead to 95-89.
Davis was fouled after another Gonzaga miss and made both free throws to seal the victory.

Creighton trailed by three with 1:12 remaining in regulation when Swartz converted a three-point play to tie the game at 79. Gonzaga’s Xaivian Lee was fouled with 1:11 left and made both free throws to give the Bulldogs an 81-79 lead.

Swartz hit a fadeaway jumper to tie the game at 81 with 58.8 seconds remaining. Fogle missed a jumper in the lane, and Creighton took possession with 30 seconds left. Davis launched a 3-point attempt at the buzzer, but the shot went in and out.
Creighton: Plays No. 25 Louisville in the Players Era 16 championship game Saturday night.
Gonzaga: Hosts Eastern Oregon on Tuesday.
