title: Holiday scammers hook older Americans first, then return later to drain their savings, expert warns
summary: Scammers target older Americans with recovery scams and AI deepfakes during the holidays, hitting victims nine times on average, federal authorities warn.
story: Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald highlights the FBI's ongoing crackdown on overseas scam networks to protect taxpayer-funded benefits on ‘America’s Newsroom.’

As the holiday season gets underway, scammers are targeting older Americans with costly schemes that could deplete their entire life savings, often returning to exploiting the same victim more than once.

The risk of elders falling victim to these schemes rises during the holidays. A November 2026 U.S. Secret Service public advisory shared with Fox News Digital stated that scammers consider the season one of their most profitable times of the year.

"USSS is better known for its protective mission," USSS Investigative Analyst Bre Whalen, CFE, told Fox News Digital. "Most people are unaware USSS conducts FI crimes investigations throughout the world, such as Operation Maple Star. Because of its partnerships with the banking community, we've developed close contacts over time."
Why holidays are lucrative for scammers
Federal authorities warn that scammers exploit the holiday rush and heightened emotions as older adults shop online, track packages online, travel and donate to charities.
Senior citizens are increasingly the victims of scams, particularly during the holiday season. (iStock)

An AARP holiday survey released in November found that 84% of U.S. adults had encountered a scam or fraud attempt ahead of the holidays. Nearly 39% of those who purchased something through an online advertisement said they were scammed, according to the survey. Around 47% received fake package-delivery alerts, while 35% bought or received a gift card with a stolen balance.

Americans ages 60 and older reported around $3 billion in fraud losses in 2025, according to an October 2026 Federal Trade Commission report. The agency estimated that older victims lost as much as $119.5 billion last year, with victims reporting only a fraction of the scams.
AGING MEANS LEARNING HOW TO PREVENT COSTLY SCAMS TARGETING OLDER AMERICANS
Why older Americans are repeated targets

The Justice Department reports that scammers target older Americans an average of nine times. After taking money in an initial scheme, fraudsters often contact victims again, posing as officials promising to recover their funds.
An AARP holiday survey released in November found that 84% of U.S. adults had encountered a scam or fraud attempt ahead of the holidays. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
"Criminals will go back to where the money is," Amy Nofziger, senior director of fraud victim support at AARP's Fraud Watch Network, told Fox News Digital.
WHY IDENTITY THEFT COMES BACK FOR THE SAME PEOPLE
"It's just why some banks get robbed every single time — the same bank — because the criminals go where the money is, and older adults hold the majority of wealth in the United States."
The process can still be challenging, experts said. Winning the confidence of victims can be difficult after they’ve been targeted and scammed.
"Victims don't trust or believe what we're saying because they've been coached by these scam centers to not answer law enforcement and think we're not real," Whalen stated.
One holiday scam leads to another

The Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said that after a successful scam, some fraudsters will share victims' personal information on the black market. This allows other criminals to target the same person, but with different schemes.
A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?

For instance, when an older shopper places an order for a fake Black Friday ad or donates to a fraudulent holiday charity site, scammers take their information and place them on "sucker lists." The lists mark these victims as easy targets, with repeated attacks that could ultimately wipe out their life savings.

"Criminals are very adept at sharing information," Nofziger said. "A lot of these criminals don't work in isolation. They work in crime rings. Perhaps Criminal A steals from a victim on a Monday, and then five Mondays later, they give or sell that information to Criminal B to try to manipulate them on another scam, knowing they still might have resources available to steal."
"Criminals will go back to where the money is," warned Amy Nofziger, senior director of fraud victim support at AARP's Fraud Watch Network. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
FAKE FEDERAL AGENTS PUSH SENIORS TO TURN SAVINGS INTO GOLD BARS FOR COURIERS TO COLLECT
Recovery scams bring criminals back
Promises to recover stolen money or lost funds are one of the most damaging schemes to older Americans during the holiday season.

After a victim loses money, another scammer may call and claim to work for a government agency, or pose as an attorney or a fraud-recovery investigator. The caller then promises to investigate the crime, find the money and get a refund.
SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO
Fraudsters will also exploit tax and financial deadlines while pushing victims to wire an immediate "processing fee" before Dec. 31 to recover lost funds or unlock a refund.
Federal authorities warn that legitimate agencies never require upfront fees to recover stolen funds, but victims often fall prey to these schemes when they become outraged and want swift justice.

"For the initial victim, they're so angry, they're so upset, they want to get justice for this," Nofziger said. "They think that this is their way out, oftentimes not really understanding that it's just a secondary scam that's happening."
Scam texts can be especially dangerous for older adults with memory issues, turning a single tap into costly purchases or recurring charges. (Ute Grabowsky/Photothek via Getty Images)
AI holiday traps
Scammers are exploiting holiday fears with AI-generated emergency calls that mimic relatives and payment-app requests designed to steal money.

One scheme, known as the "grandparent scam," happens when criminals pull videos from social media accounts or public sources. They clone a relative's voice using artificial intelligence, and then pose as loved ones asking for emergency funds or Christmas cash.
Fraudsters are also using full AI video deepfakes, sometimes posing as physicians, to bilk funds from unsuspecting older Americans.
In December 2025, an 82-year-old Florida grandmother lost more than $200,000 to an AI deepfake scam, when someone pretended to be a doctor in a Facebook community focused on autism.
The grandmother said she had been saving her money for her autistic grandson’s future, and the fake physician urged people to invest.
Nofziger urges families to discuss these scams openly, while taking steps to avoid victim-blaming. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
"It looked completely real — his face, his voice, everything," she told First Coast News. "I wanted to save more money for my grandson, and so I fell for it hook, line and sinker."
"I got very emotional and so angry with myself that I had difficulty functioning. I lost 20 pounds and couldn’t sleep because it went through my mind over and over again."
How loved ones can help
Shame can keep victims silent, which ends up leaving them vulnerable to repeat attacks, Nofziger said, adding that victims may feel guilt for being scammed in the first place.
Nofziger urges families to discuss these scams openly, while taking steps to avoid victim-blaming.

"The scammers are masters of manipulation, and they know how to manipulate human beings and their feelings," she said. "The victim has been manipulated and technically, you know, brainwashed by this criminal for months and years."

"It took years to get there. It might take a long time to unravel that emotional grasp that these criminals have on their victims... The person who should be embarrassed is the criminal who stole the money from them."
She added that unraveling a scammer's manipulative hold takes time and outside support, whether from local law enforcement, support groups or counselors.
SEND US A TIP
Can victims get their money back?

Victims are urged to contact their banks, payment providers, and local law enforcement immediately if they suspect fraud. Banks can possibly stop or recall some transfers, but it largely depends on the payment method and how quickly they report the scam.
GOT A TIP?

Cryptocurrency, gift cards, cash and gold are more difficult to recover since criminals typically know how to move them quickly. Once a victim is ensnared, scammers can move the money through multiple accounts and intermediaries, such as money mules, to hide transactions.
USSS advises victims to immediately report any suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
"Current fraud info is provided real time; in most cases we have just minutes to act on this information before the fraud is committed," Whalen said.
"We work closely with local police and banking industry, although we are still working to make efforts to partner with some of the banking sector that is slow to respond to real-time data."
Anyone of any age, including non-members, can contact the free AARP Fraud Watch Network Helpline at 877-908-3360 for guidance, support groups and to learn about other steps to take.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Victims and families can also contact the National Elder Fraud Hotline at 833-FRAUD-11 or visit the Justice Department’s Elder Justice Initiative website.

title: Explosion near Afghan school kills at least 10, injures 110 as children rushed to hospital
summary: The Taliban Interior Ministry says a school explosion in Kunar province killed 10 and injured 110, with video showing children rushed to hospital.
story: Afghan residents rushed wounded children to the hospital after an explosion near a school in Afghanistan's Kunar province killed at least 10 people and injured at least 110 others. Credit: Reuters.
An explosion at a school in northeast Afghanistan has killed at least 10 people and injured 110 more, according to a spokesperson for the Taliban's Interior Ministry and the BBC.
Early reports indicate that the explosion happened at a building storing explosives for mining near the school, Taliban spokesman Abdul Mateen Qani said in a statement.
Qani claimed the explosion was caused by "negligence and carelessness at an explosives depot belonging to mining companies near the school."

The explosion took place in Afghanistan's Kunar province, a subdivision that borders Pakistan and is home to a significant mining operation, in the Asadabad district, which sits right on the Kunar River that separates western Pakistan from eastern Afghanistan.
TALIBAN REPORTEDLY STRIPS WOMEN OF THEIR NAMES IN AFGHAN PROVINCE, NOW BEING CALLED 'GOAT' OR 'GRANDMOTHER'
FILE - An aerial view shows the Kunar river running past a hillside in Kunar province on September 14, 2025. (WAKIL KOHSAR/AFP via Getty Images)
Qani also said that authorities are investigating the explosion and will release more details following a government inquiry.
Chaotic video from the aftermath shows Afghans pulling bloodied children from cars and rushing them into Asadabad Provincial Hospital.

Afghan schoolchildren and other victims injured in an explosion receive medical treatment at a hospital in Asadabad, in Afghanistan's Kunar province on Nov. 28, 2026. An explosion near a school in Afghanistan's eastern Kunar province killed at least 10 people and injured at least 110 others, officials said. (Aimal Zahir / AFP via Getty Images)
Sami-ul-Haq Haq Bayan, director of information for the Kunar province, also confirmed the blast.
The incident marks the second such explosion in Afghanistan that impacted young students in recent months.

title: Zelenskyy compares Putin to Hitler as Trump pushes to end Ukraine war: 'He's an aggressor and a killer'
summary: Volodomyr Zelenskyy says Vladmir Putin is "an aggressor and a killer," comparing him to Adolf Hitler and arguing he cannot be President Trump's friend.
story: President Donald Trump addresses foreign policy on Thanksgiving, calling on President Vladimir Putin to pull back aggression. Trump doubles down on support for Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy compared Russian President Vladimir Putin to Adolf Hitler on Thursday amid President Donald Trump's ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

"Of course, it's up to President of the United States, but it's strange. He's (Putin) an aggressor and a killer. He can't be a friend. It just cannot be," Zelenskyy told the British Broadcasting Company (BBC) during an interview that aired Thursday.
"It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War, that he's a good friend. No, he is not a friend," Zelenskyy continued.
Trump used the word friend to describe Putin while meeting with the Russian president during a trilateral summit in China on Nov. 19.

Russia's President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump shake hands during a meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 19, 2026. (Vyacheslav PROKOFYEV / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
ZELENSKYY PRESSES US FOR EXPANDED RUSSIA TALKS AS KUSHNER ANNOUNCES BREAKTHROUGH

Trump entered a room where Putin was waiting and said, "Who is he? He's my friend," before shaking Putin's hand. He later posted a photo to Truth Social of the pair shaking hands with the caption "My Friend."
Zelenskyy further criticized the United States, claiming the U.S. was sending Ukraine signals similar to those he had been getting from Russia.

"We need more progress. This is what we need. We need American position to be American position. We don't need signals, I mean, that are from the United States, which we can get from Russia," he told the BBC.

"It's not about Russia or not Russia," he added. "They have to put pressure on the situation. The situation is … Russia is [the] aggressor. So that's why they have to do it. That's why they are mediators. It's not about comfortable talks. It's about a strong country who can pressure because this country has power and respect."
KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

FILE - Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks during a press briefing on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City on September 23, 2025. Zelenskyy accused the U.S. of "help[ing]" more in the Middle East. (Photo by LEONARDO MUNOZ/AFP via Getty Images)
Zelenskyy also expressed frustration that the U.S. has focused much of its foreign policy bandwidth on the Middle East during the Iran war rather than on Europe.
"It's a pity they made a focus on the Middle East and they helped them more, but it's their choice," he said.

The war between Russia and Ukraine has been raging for nearly five years. Starting when Russian troops invaded eastern Ukraine, the war has now racked up well over 1 million casualties between Russia and Ukraine, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies.
MIKE WALTZ WARNS KREMLIN FACES 'UNSUSTAINABLE' LOSSES APPROACHING WWII SCALE AS TRUMP SEEKS DEAL
A recent report from Russian news outlets estimated that Russia has lost at least 700,000 troops. CSIS estimates that Russia's casualty numbers are double those of Ukraine's.
Despite the apparent mismatch in casualties, Russia now holds portions of Ukrainian territory and may be poised to keep them after the war's conclusion, a possibility Trump acknowledged.
TRUMP RUSSIA DEAL COULD FUEL PUTIN'S WAR, EX-NATO COMMANDER WARNS AS ZELENSKYY SAYS 'NYET'
FILE - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (L) meets with US President Donald Trump (R) at the White House during his visit to Washington, D.C, United States on July 28, 2026.
"They're gonna end up with a little bit different shaped Ukraine," Trump told Ross Douthat of CBS' "60 Minutes."
Trump also told CBS that he believed the war is going to end soon.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
He also told reporters on Thursday that he's pushing each side to make a deal.
"We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing," Trump said.

"I could walk in and say, ‘I don’t like you!’ and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelenskyy and Putin. The biggest problem with that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other," the president added.
Fox News Digital contacted the White House for comment.

title: Taliban reportedly strips women of their names in Afghan province, now being called 'goat' or 'grandmother'
summary: The Taliban reportedly banned women's names from official records in an Afghan province, five years after reclaiming power amid Biden's chaotic withdrawal.
story: Afghan women operate underground beauty salons, teach girls in secret schools and coach children in soccer despite sweeping restrictions imposed by the Taliban. (The Associated Press)

The Taliban have reportedly banned the use of women's names in official documents in a northern Afghan province, with some women being referred to by degrading animal names, according to a report by Spanish newspaper El País.

The latest assault on women's rights under Taliban rule reportedly extends to medical records and prescriptions in Afghanistan's Balkh province, raising fears that the restrictions could spread nationwide.

Healthcare workers and other public employees have been instructed to address women as "Bibi," meaning grandmother or old woman, according to reporting by Afghan news outlet Zan Times and The Guardian cited by El País.
MOSCOW, TALIBAN FORGE MILITARY ALLIANCE IN POWER GRAB AFTER US AFGHANISTAN EXIT: REPORTS
Burqa-clad women carry their children while walking along a street in Afghanistan's Kandahar province on Nov. 23, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

Afghan women's rights activist Lalah Osmany, who is based in Germany, told El País that testimony from women, doctors and civil rights activists indicates some women are also being referred to in degrading terms such as "goat" or "cow."
"This is a systematic process of dehumanization," Osmany told the newspaper.
An Afghan activist speaking under a pseudonym confirmed the reported order to El País, although she said it had so far been ignored.

Zubaida Akbar, who directs the Afghanistan program at women's rights organization Femena, warned that the Taliban could eventually impose the ban nationwide, citing previous instances in which local restrictions were expanded across the country.
IRAN FLOGS FEMALE SINGER 74 TIMES FOR PERFORMING WITHOUT HIJAB IN VIRAL YOUTUBE CONCERT
An Afghan burqa-clad woman peels grapes for her child along a street in Kandahar on Nov. 17, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
Femena has counted more than 144 decrees restricting Afghan women's rights, according to El País.

Girls have been barred from studying beyond age 12, while women have been shut out of most professions and subjected to restrictions on speaking in public, the newspaper reported.Some Afghan women have resorted to running underground businesses and secret schools in defiance of Taliban restrictions, according to Associated Press reporting published Nov. 17.
IRAN TO EXECUTE FIRST FEMALE PROTESTER TIED TO ANTI-REGIME UNREST
Afghan burqa-clad women stand in a queue as they wait to receive food aid from a non-governmental organization (NGO) at a gymnasium in Kabul on Jan. 17, 2023. (Wakil Kohsar/AFP via Getty Images)
One Kabul beauty salon owner, whose identity was concealed for her safety, reopened her business after authorities raided her previous salon and confiscated her equipment.
"But now, they won’t even allow that; for women in Afghanistan, working has become a crime," she told the AP.
An assistant teacher at a secret school in Kabul described living in constant fear of arrest.
"We are absolutely terrified of that possibility," she told the AP.

Mohammad Aslam, a spokesman for the Taliban's Ministry for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, defended the broader restrictions in comments to the AP, saying women could conduct business and social affairs provided they adhered to Islamic Sharia law and existing laws.
Osmany also warned that the reported naming ban could endanger female patients by increasing the risk of medical errors if prescriptions and medical records are filed under identical names.

Afghan women already face severe barriers to medical care under Taliban rule, including restrictions on male doctors treating female patients and bans on women pursuing medical training, according to El País.
In 2017, Osmany launched a campaign to have Afghan women's names included on official documents, including their children's birth certificates.
ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'

An Afghan man holds up a yellow plastic barrel in a crowd near armed Taliban fighters on a military vehicle during celebrations for the fifth anniversary of the Taliban's takeover in Herat, Afghanistan, on Aug. 15, 2026. (Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)
Despite receiving death threats from extremists, her campaign helped secure a change in 2020 allowing mothers' names to be voluntarily included on such documents. That progress was short-lived.

The Taliban swept back into power in August 2021 as the U.S.-backed Afghan government collapsed amid then-President Joe Biden's chaotic military withdrawal, leaving the country once again under the control of Islamist extremists.
The withdrawal drew widespread condemnation after 13 American service members, mostly Marines, were killed in an ISIS-K terrorist attack during the evacuation from Kabul.
Biden faced further backlash from Gold Star families after checking his watch during the dignified transfer of fallen American troops at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware.
Five years later, Afghan women and girls have seen hard-won freedoms stripped away under Taliban rule. Now, activists warn, even their very identities are under threat.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Calling a woman by her real name in Afghanistan is an act of resistance," Osmany told El País.
Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Tiny English village battles government over migrant housing plan amid crime fears for women
summary: Piddington villagers voted 285-26 to secede from the UK after learning plans would house over 1,200 male asylum seekers at MoD Bicester nearby.
story: Local councillor Michael Nixon says residents of the 350-person village were shocked by plans to house 1,250 men nearby without consultation. (Video: Reuters.)
A rural Oxfordshire village of just over 350 people is taking on the British government, finding itself at the center of a national debate over immigration and public safety.

Residents of Piddington, a small community about 10 miles from the famous Oxford University and known more for its rural setting and centuries-old parish church than political activism, voted overwhelmingly in September to secede from the United Kingdom in a symbolic referendum. The 285-26 vote came after residents learned Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government planned to house more than 1,200 male asylum seekers at a former Ministry of Defence base in Bicester — less than a mile from the village.

What began as a local planning dispute has since become one of Britain's most closely watched immigration battles. The controversy intensified earlier this month when the government approved plans for the asylum accommodation center despite objections from local officials, residents and the Thames Valley Police and Crime Commissioner.
WHO IS ANDY BURNHAM? BRITAIN'S NEW PRIME MINISTER AND LONGTIME TRUMP CRITIC

Local residents pose with a "Principality of Piddington" sign in the village of Piddington, Oxfordshire, after they voted overwhelmingly to become an independent state in a symbolic "referendum". The village of around 350 residents held the vote after the Government said it wanted to set up a migrant camp close by. Wednesday Sept.16, 2026.  (Joe Giddens/PA Wire POLITICS via AP)

"The Piddington situation reflects a political choice by the Burnham government to start locating asylum seekers across the whole country, to share the burden equally," Alan Mendoza, executive director of the Henry Jackson Society, told Fox News Digital. He added that most locations selected to house migrants "do not vote Labour usually," adding that some residents view the policy "as a form of political punishment."

On Nov. 12, Housing and Communities Secretary Angela Rayner approved planning permission for the project, despite opposition from local residents and officials. The government argued the facility is needed as part of its broader effort to reform the UK's asylum system and expand the use of alternative accommodation sites.
200,000 SMALL BOAT ARRIVALS LOOM AMID UK RAISING THREAT LEVEL TO ‘SEVERE’ FOLLOWING RECENT TERROR ATTACK

A security guard looks out from the main gates of MoD Bicester, after Communities Secretary Angela Rayner approved full planning permission, to convert the former MoD site near the village of Piddington in Oxfordshire, into accommodation for more than 1,200 detained asylum seekers. Ministers have faced angry opposition from villagers over the plans, who even made a symbolic attempt to declare the village independent of the rest of the country. Friday Nov.13, 2026.  (Joe Giddens/Press Association POLITICS (Press Association via AP Images))

"I think it's fair to say we were shocked by the news," Michael Nixon, a member of the Piddington Parish Council, told Reuters at the time of the decision, "because we are a very small village. We have a total of 350 residents, including 46 children. We don't have too much else in the village. There's no shop. There's no pub. You know, we are just a small rural community, and to have the thought of 1,250 lone men on our doorstep, without any consultation, without any thought about how that could be absorbed into our village, really shocked us."

A Home Office spokesperson said the government is "working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country" and moving away from the use of asylum hotels. The spokesperson added that former military sites, such as MoD Bicester, are designed to be "self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to minimize the impact on the local community."
Not everyone is convinced the government's assurances will be enough.

An aerial view of Piddington in Oxfordshire, as Communities Secretary Angela Rayner has approved full planning permission, to convert a Ministry of Defence site near the Oxfordshire village into accommodation for more than 1,200 detained asylum seekers. Ministers have faced angry opposition from villagers over the plans, who even made a symbolic attempt to declare the village independent from the rest of the country.  (Joe Giddens/Press Association POLITICS)

In an Oct. 16 letter to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, Thames Valley Police and Crime Commissioner Matthew Barber warned that local residents had "genuine concerns" about the project’s impact on "their safety and security." He added that "given the open nature of the site we know that there will be an increased risk to the public."

Barber went further, writing: "We must expect an increase in crime as a result of the Government's proposals… it is naïve to consider that such a large population of single men will not bring with it a greater risk of violent and sexual offenses."
EU ADMITS IT ‘DIDN’T HAVE CONTROL’ ON MIGRATION AS BLOC RUSHES CRACKDOWN AHEAD OF NEW RULES

In an interview on GB News last month, Piddington resident Christina Gower said villagers had been advised by rural policing personnel that officers could take up to 45 minutes to respond to an emergency call and that the best thing residents could do in the meantime was to "run and hide." Thames Valley Police has not publicly confirmed that guidance.
Mendoza said, "It is understandable [residents] feel abandoned when they lack the enforcement mechanisms to deal with potential criminal outbreaks in what are usually very peaceful areas."

Andy Burnham delivers his inaugural speech as U.K.'s new Prime Minister on July 20, 2026, in London, England. The Member of Parliament for Makerfield becomes the UK's 59th Prime Minister, succeeding Sir Keir Starmer, who resigned as leader of the Labour Party and Prime Minister in June.  (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

Government planning documents show officials considered concerns about community safety, policing demand and the safety of women and girls before approving the project. The documents state that security measures would help mitigate those concerns, but acknowledge they "cannot eliminate all risk."
The Home Office said that while planning permission has been granted, a final decision on whether the MoD Bicester site will ultimately be used for asylum accommodation has not yet been made.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In the meantime, residents of what parish chairman Tim McNally declared the "Principality of Piddington" remain defiant, saying they have no intention of backing down. What began as a local dispute over a former military base has evolved into a national test case in Britain's ongoing battle over immigration, public safety and who bears the burden of accommodating asylum seekers.
The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: US military disables tanker ship attempting to slip through Iran blockade on Thanksgiving Day
summary: CENTCOM video shows a U.S. strike disabling a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after it tried to evade the naval blockade of all Iranian ports.
story: According to U.S. Central Command, a tanker ship attempting to run the naval Iran blockade was disabled after its crew refused to listen to multiple warnings.
A U.S. military aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it tried to evade the naval blockade of all Iranian ports, which has been in effect since mid-July.

The Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer left Bandar Abbas, a major port city on Iran's southern coast, before the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) fired precision munitions at the ship's stern, destroying its propulsion.
A video released by the military shows a projectile hitting the back of the ship and causing an explosion. The civilian crew was unharmed in the strike, CENTCOM said.
So far, U.S. forces have redirected 158 compliant commercial vessels and disabled six that refused to comply.

The moment a U.S. military aircraft struck a Palau-flagged commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman on Nov. 26, 2026. The ship left Bandar Abbas and tried to slip through the U.S. naval blockade. (U.S. Central Command)
TRUMP DARES IRAN TO BREACH US PORT BLOCKADE AS TEHRAN REPORTEDLY READIES 14 OIL TANKERS
President Donald Trump said Thursday, while celebrating Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, that victory in the Iran war would come "whenever I want it."

"We have victory at hand. It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said in a phone call to U.S. service members.
Trump also praised U.S. troops for their role in preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump speak with participate in calls with U.S. service members from Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving Day, on Nov. 26, 2026 in Palm Beach, Florida. (Daniel Heuer/Getty Images)
TRUMP PAUSES TURKEY PARDON TO SALUTE US TROOPS GUARDING STRAIT OF HORMUZ: 'WATCH OVER AND PROTECT'

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you," he said.
Trump added that the U.S. has launched 150 missiles to intercept threats targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Asked whether Moscow and Beijing are providing Iran with intelligence to help it target U.S. military bases, Trump minimized the likelihood and said China was not heavily involved. He maintained that both countries are interested in helping the U.S. bring the war to a close.
Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz are visible near the beach of Bandar Abbas, Iran, August 27, 2026. (Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency))
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Trump said that if the U.S. were to resume strikes, CENTCOM forces would "absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain," an underground complex near Iran's Natanz enrichment complex.
The likelihood of Iran agreeing to a deal proposed by the U.S. is low, Trump also told reporters.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Putin's grip on Crimea tested amid major blackout as Zelenskyy warns of looming Russian strike
summary: A massive blackout crippled Crimea, testing Vladimir Putin's grip as outages hit Sevastopol and Simferopol and Zelenskyy warned of a new Russian strike.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Benjamin Hall reports on Ukraine's major strike on the Kerch Bridge in Crimea. Hall details Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's warning to Russia and reports on upcoming peace negotiations led by top Trump aides Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

Russian President Vladimir Putin's control over Crimea faced renewed pressure Thursday as a massive blackout crippled the Russian-occupied peninsula, disrupting public transport and leaving people without heat, according to reports.

The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine.

Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post.
PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE
Residential buildings at night during a power outage across Crimea. (Alexey Pavlishak/Reuters)
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence suggested that Russia was preparing to target the country's energy infrastructure, logistics networks and essential services.

"Unfortunately, the Russians are already completing preparations for a new massive strike," Zelenskyy wrote on X Thursday following a coordination meeting. "According to intelligence, energy facilities and logistics infrastructure, as well as essential services facilities in cities and communities, will once again be the targets."
The Ukrainian leader also urged residents to remain vigilant, warning of renewed missile attacks.

"In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address Thursday, according to Reuters. "And in Russia, they should know that we will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike."

In Crimea, Russian-controlled electricity provider Sevastopolenergo said that Sevastopol had lost power, while electricity restrictions affected Simferopol, Kerch, Alushta and Yevpatoria, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.
ZELENSKYY SAYS RUSSIA STRIKES HOMETOWN, CRITICIZES PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING

Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are shown in a side-by-side photo illustration as discussions continue over the future of Ukraine and a potential settlement to the war. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP; Christian Bruna/Getty Images)
Streetcar services were also suspended in Yevpatoria and buses replaced trolleybuses on some routes in Simferopol. Parts of Kerch were also reportedly left without heating.
Russian-installed authorities had issued air raid alerts Thursday morning amid reports of explosions.
The blackout is the latest in a series of disruptions that have hit Crimea since late October, with Russian authorities blaming damage to power infrastructure.
The disruptions come amid mounting pressure on Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014 and has since used as a military and logistics hub for its operations against Ukraine.

The Kerch Strait Bridge, which connects the peninsula to mainland Russia, serves as a critical transportation link for Russian forces and has been targeted by Ukraine since Putin launched his invasion in 2022.
KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION
A view shows the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea, which was targeted in an explosion by Ukraine on Tuesday, June 3, 2025. (Alexey Pavlishak/Reuters)
The bridge was built after the Russian annexation and opened in 2018, serving as a symbol of Moscow's control over the peninsula.

Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko also said seven people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital that damaged a shopping center and two other buildings, Reuters reported.

Zelenskyy also called for additional air defense assistance Thursday, emphasizing the need for interceptors for Patriot air defense systems and National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile Systems (NASAMS).

"I expect a report from Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry on the results of its communication with our partners regarding the supply of air defenses — interceptors for Patriots and NASAMS are the key priority," Zelenskyy wrote.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
It was the second time this week Zelenskyy had warned of preparations for another major Russian attack, according to Reuters.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Iran accuses Zelenskyy of 'false flag' Kuwait drone strike op to get Trump's attention
summary: A former Iran nuclear adviser claimed Thursday the Kuwait drone attack was a Ukrainian "false flag" staged to get President Donald Trump's attention.
story: Ret. Navy Vice Adm. Kevin Donegan, former Navy 5th Fleet commander, says the Middle East’s actors have changed ‘dramatically’ since he held command on ‘The Story.’

A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team accused Ukraine on Thursday of orchestrating a deadly drone attack in Kuwait to prove its worth to President Donald Trump, as Tehran continued to deny responsibility.

And while Kuwaiti and Italian officials blamed Iran for the strike, which killed two Italian defense technicians and wounded two others, Iran’s embassy in Rome warned against "false flag" operations it said were aimed at widening the Persian Gulf conflict and now drawing Europe into the crisis.

Mohammad Marandi, who served as an adviser during talks with the U.S. in Pakistan and has been dubbed Iran's "English-language mouthpiece," claimed Ukrainian forces were operating across the Middle East, including in northern Iraq and Syria, also in remarks reported by the Fars News Agency, which is affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
IRAN TARGETS US AIR BASE IN KUWAIT AFTER US DEFENSIVE STRIKES AMID CRITICISM FROM GULF STATES
Smoke rises after a reported Iranian strike near the U.S. Embassy in Kuwait City on Mar. 2, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"It is widely believed in Iran that the attack on Kuwait was a false flag operation, likely carried out by the Ukrainian regime, because its operatives are now present across the region, including in northern Iraq and Syria. Ukraine aims to demonstrate its potential to Trump," Marandi said on X.

Fars also cited a security source who claimed Ukrainian operatives had deployed thousands of drones and other unmanned aircraft in several Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq's Kurdistan region, according to Iran International.

Kuwait's Defense Ministry said falling debris from the interception of Iranian drones struck a military facility Thursday, initially wounding four people. Two Italian nationals later died of their injuries.
A Kuwaiti national and a Pakistani national were also wounded and taken to a hospital for treatment. The ministry did not disclose the facility's precise location.
Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed that the two Italian nationals were employees of Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian subsidiary of German defense manufacturer Rheinmetall.
"An explosion caused by a drone attack ... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working," the ministry said in a statement.
The victims were identified as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, of Formia, Italy, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, of Rome, Italian news agency ANSA reported.
EUROPE ASSASSINATION SCHEME EMERGES AS IRAN DENIES DC 'DIRTY BOMB' PLOT AMID TRUMP WARNING
Kuwait’s civil aviation authority released surveillance footage it says shows an Iranian drone crashing into the country’s international airport. (CIVIL AVIATION KUWAIT)
The men had been performing maintenance on detection antennas for the Skyguard air defense system.
Iran's embassy in Rome rejected allegations that Tehran was responsible for the attack, warning of alleged efforts to draw European countries into the Middle East conflict.

"The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran also draws the international community's attention to 'false flag' activities and operations aimed at expanding the scope of the conflict, linking disputes in other regions to the Persian Gulf crisis, drawing Europe into the crisis, and exacerbating the current critical situation, and calls on everyone to remain vigilant in this regard."
Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he had spoken with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and offered to cooperate in an investigation into the deadly incident.

"In calls with my Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts, expressed condolences over deaths of Italian citizens in Kuwait," Araghchi wrote. "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war.
"We stand ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident," he added.
TOP GULF OFFICIAL OFFERS GLIMMER OF HOPE ON TRUMP-IRAN NUCLEAR TALKS AS THREAT OF WAR HANGS OVER REGION

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi speaks during a joint press conference with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan (not pictured) in Tehran, Iran, Nov. 30, 2025. (Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via Reuters)
Kuwait, a key U.S. ally in the Persian Gulf, has repeatedly come under Iranian attack since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran on Feb. 28.

Ukraine has deployed drone specialists and interceptor drones to the Middle East to help defend against Iranian attacks, expanding its regional defense cooperation by sharing technology and military expertise developed during its war with Russia.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in March that Kyiv had sent interceptor drones and specialists to help protect U.S. military installations in Jordan at Washington's request.
Ukraine also announced that teams of military specialists had been deployed to Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia to help defend against Iranian drone attacks.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Ukraine has the greatest experience in the world in countering attack drones," Zelenskyy said in March, adding that "without our experience, it will be very difficult for the Gulf region, the entire Middle East, and partners in Europe and America to build strong protection."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: UK shields fighter jets, contacts reservists in Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
summary: Wes Streeting says the United Kingdom is contacting former service members to update its strategic reserve as Russian sabotage rises across Europe.
story: British Ambassador to the U.S. Sir Christian Turner discusses U.S. strikes against Iran and President Donald Trump's proposal to end aid to Israel, on 'The Story.'

The United Kingdom is bolstering its military readiness amid growing threats from Russia, contacting former service members to assess its reserves as the Royal Air Force reportedly strengthens defenses against potential drone attacks.

Britain's Ministry of Defence has written to former service members to verify their contact information and military skills to ensure the country is prepared for a national emergency or potential conflict, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting confirmed Friday.
The outreach comes as the International Institute for Strategic Studies warned Thursday that suspected Russian-directed sabotage across Europe could trigger a "mass-casualty event."
NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL
RAF Typhoon Fighter Jets operate from RAF Coningsby. (Ryan Jenkinson/Getty Images)

The think tank found that sabotage incidents rose 16% in the year through September 2026, with Germany and Poland accounting for more than half of the cases. Researchers warned that a major attack could spark calls for retaliation and divide European governments.
"I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," Streeting told BBC Radio 4's "Today" program.
"You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," he said.
Streeting said the government needed updated records of its strategic reserve in case former service members were called upon to respond to a domestic disaster or overseas conflict.
He cited Russian incursions into Polish airspace, suspected Russian-sponsored sabotage across Europe and Iran-linked threats to British military bases.

Last week, a suspected Russian projectile landed in eastern Poland about 60 miles from a British-led military exercise. The incident happened the same day Britain's defense secretary and chief of the air staff visited troops.
INSIDE THE PENTAGON'S DOOMSDAY PLAN TO KEEP AMERICA FIGHTING IF GLOBAL WAR ERUPTS

Soldiers in action as the British Army demonstrates the latest and future technology used in operations across the globe on the Salisbury Plain training area in Salisbury, England. (Finnbarr Webster/Getty Images)

"And so against that backdrop, against that threat environment, the government and the country has to be ready to face down those risks," Streeting said. "Because the more ready we are, the less likely we are to find ourselves in a conflict, in a war. That is my goal. That is the goal of this government."

The Ministry of Defence said in a news release it was contacting thousands of former military personnel this week as part of a drive to "strengthen the UK’s readiness and deliver on recommendations made in the Strategic Defence Review."

"Service Chiefs are writing to members of the Strategic Reserve, asking them to stay connected and update their details, providing Defence with a better understanding of the skills and experience it could draw upon if needed."
"In the coming months, Strategic Reservists will have the opportunity to volunteer for training and exercises, such as the UK’s participation in NATO’s flagship Steadfast Defender next spring."

The outreach marks the first time since the Cold War that Britain's defense ministry has contacted reservists on such a scale to encourage participation in military exercises, according to The Telegraph.
TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE

Russian President Vladimir Putin chairs a meeting aboard the missile cruiser Varyag in Russia's far eastern Sakhalin region on Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. Putin previously said Russia is not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe. (Reuters)

Meanwhile, Britain's domestic intelligence agency, MI5, and the defense ministry have reportedly warned British companies supplying military equipment to Ukraine that they could be targeted by Russian saboteurs.
The Royal Air Force is strengthening security at military bases, using hardened aircraft shelters and installing anti-drone netting to protect exposed fighter jets, according to The Times.
The measures follow Iranian threats against military bases in England that prompted tighter security and the relocation of U.S. military aircraft.
Suspected drone incursions over European airfields have also heightened concerns about Russian aggression.
"We take the security of our bases, equipment and personnel very seriously and are always adapting to counter any potential threats," a Ministry of Defence spokesperson told Fox News Digital.
US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING
The main gate of RAF Fairford is pictured on September 27, 2026, in Fairford, United Kingdom. (David Bown/Getty Images)
"This includes investing an additional £470 million to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection, surveillance and counter-drone capabilities.
"We have already invested £15 million in drone and counter-drone technology and introduced restricted airspace over 44 critical Defence sites."

The developments come as President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, signaling a shift in tone toward the Russian leader, whom he called a friend last week.
Trump said he made the request during a meeting with Putin in China last week, adding that he believed it could help secure a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.
Trump's comments came a day after he hosted NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte in Florida. The two leaders issued a joint statement urging Russia not to expand its war in Ukraine.

"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Trump said on Truth Social.

title: Ukrainian intelligence says North Korea paused missile deliveries to Russia amid friction over South Korea
summary: North Korea paused ballistic missile and artillery shipments to Russia after friction over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian intelligence said.
story: Escalating tensions in the Ukraine war take center stage as NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte prepares to meet with President Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago. Speaking with Brian Kilmeade on 'Fox & Friends,' Rutte highlights unsustainable Russian military casualties, which exceeded 50,000 dead or wounded in October alone. He also addresses concerns about the conflict spreading further into Europe.

North Korea has temporarily halted shipments of ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia following diplomatic friction between the two allies over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian military intelligence said Thursday.

According to Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency, North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze on KN-23 ballistic missile and artillery deliveries last month after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko suggested Moscow would help de-escalate tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang, Reuters reported.
Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy toward South Korea, GUR said, though Reuters noted it could not independently verify the report or confirm public remarks from either official.
PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS

Russian President Vladimir Putin meets Jo Yong Won, chairman of the Standing Committee of North Korea's Supreme People's Assembly, in Moscow, Russia, Nov. 16, 2026. (Sputnik/Valeriy Sharifulin/Pool via Reuters)

The reported pause also suspends Russian military flights over North Korea and stalls a Kremlin request to expand North Korea's troop deployment in Russia from roughly 8,500 to 50,000, according to the outlet.
Rudenko, who oversees Asian relations, said last month that Seoul had signaled interest in normalizing ties and resuming direct flights with Moscow once the Ukraine war ends.

Despite the reported freeze, North Korean troops remain active in Russia, with 11th Corps units serving in the Kursk region and a missile unit operating in Voronezh since mid-summer, GUR said. Russian President Vladimir Putin also hosted top Kim Jong Un aide Jo Yong Won at the Kremlin last week, where both men reportedly praised bilateral cooperation.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on social media Thursday that Moscow is "completing preparations for a new massive strike" on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services.
A firefighter works to extinguish a fire at a private house following a Russian air attack in Kharkiv, Ukraine, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Andrii Marienko)
TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

Crews are already working to restore power in six regions after overnight Russian missile and drone strikes damaged an apartment building, a hospital and businesses, according to Zelenskyy, who also renewed appeals for U.S.-made Patriot air defense interceptors.

In Washington, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday that he urged Putin during talks in China to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."

Russia’s President Vladimir Putin meets with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and Federal Acquisition Service Commissioner Josh Gruenbaum at the Kremlin in Moscow on Jan. 22, 2026. (Alexander Kazakov/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

U.S. envoy Jared Kushner, who is mediating talks with Steve Witkoff, said on the "MD Meets" podcast that Putin has "shown restraint" by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons, though negotiations remain deadlocked over Ukrainian territory.

Ukrainian forces also struck a Russian military airfield and an oil pumping facility overnight, while Russia claimed it intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones.

title: FlyDubai to resume Tel Aviv flights following attempted hijacking incident
summary: FlyDubai will resume flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, on Dec. 3 under new security arrangements after the Sept. 30 attempted hijacking, reports say.
story: FlyDubai passenger Tal joins 'Fox & Friends' to detail the terrifying hijacking attempt where hero Israeli passengers rushed the cockpit to stop an attacker from taking control of the aircraft. Tal describes the chaotic scene, the quick actions of Captain Smit Machchhar and how passengers worked together to secure the plane.

FlyDubai announced Thursday it will resume flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, next week, ending a suspension in place following an attempted hijacking incident in late September, according to media reports.
A source familiar with the matter told The Times of Israel that the airline is being allowed back into Israeli airspace "under new security arrangements."

The development comes after Transportation Minister Miri Regev decided this week that FlyDubai flights to Israel can resume pending clearance from Shin Bet, Mossad and Israel's National Security Council, the outlet reported.

A FlyDubai spokesperson told Reuters that the flights will begin again on Dec. 3. FlyDubai flights to Israel have been suspended since FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 on Sept. 30, when a co-pilot allegedly attacked his captain.
FLYDUBAI CO-PILOT ALLEGEDLY PLANNED TO CRASH ISRAEL-BOUND JET AT BEN GURION AIRPORT
A Flydubai Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft prepares for landing at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport on Sept. 30, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
That plane was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where it made a safe landing.

"Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian captain of FlyDubai Flight 1073, fought back after being stabbed in the cockpit," according to the Israel Foreign Ministry. "Despite being severely injured, he managed to unlock the cockpit door – allowing Israeli passengers and the Emirati crew to intervene and save all the passengers."
FLYDUBAI PILOT SHOWED WORLD 'THE HIGHEST FORM OF COURAGE,' INDIA'S PM SAYS
Capt. Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who allegedly was attacked on a FlyDubai plane heading to Israel on Sept. 30, 2026. (Israel Foreign Ministry)

Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 reported that Hamam al-Hammami told investigators he intended to continue Flight FZ1073 toward Israel as though nothing was wrong, obtain the necessary clearances to approach Ben Gurion Airport and then crash the aircraft into a building or another plane at the airport.

Israeli passenger Haim Lazarovich, who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia during a FlyDubai flight, arrives at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel, Sept. 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Ariel Schalit)

UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said investigators determined that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act by attacking the captain with a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft.
Fox News Digital's Bradford Betz contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Bangkok oil refinery explosion injures at least 9, Thailand company monitoring air quality
summary: Nine people are injured, three critically, after an explosion at Bangchak Corporation's oil refinery in Bangkok, Thailand, as residents get phone alerts.
story: An explosion at an oil refinery in Thailand's capital Bangkok send giant smoke plumes into the sky. Bangchak Corporation, which owns the facility, said the fire was extinguished within 30 minutes of the explosion. Credit: Reuters.
At least nine people have been injured in an oil refinery explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, on Thursday, with three in critical condition.
The explosion occurred at a Bangchak Corporation-owned facility, the company confirmed in a statement posted to Facebook.
The company also claimed it was able to control and extinguish a large blaze caused by the explosion within 30 minutes of the blast.
EMERGENCY CREWS RESPONDING TO MASSIVE EXPLOSION AT NEW ORLEANS-AREA OIL REFINERY: SHERIFF
Additionally, it claimed monitoring showed no reduction in normal air quality.

Smoke and flames rise from the Bangchak oil refinery following an explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 26, 2026, in this screen grab taken from a video. (Nattawut Wonghirunkonchai/Handout via Reuters)

"Since the incident occurred, the company has continuously monitored air quality in real time using automatic ambient air quality monitoring (AQM) stations, which the company has installed in the Phra Khanong, Bang Na, and Bang Nam Phueng areas to measure air quality around the refinery resulting from operations," the company wrote.
TWO INJURED AFTER EXPLOSION RIPS THROUGH CHEMICAL PLANT, SPARKING HAZMAT RESPONSE, SHELTER-IN-PLACE ORDER

"It was found that the air quality in the surrounding area of the refinery is within normal standards. Furthermore, at 5: 30 PM (17: 30 hrs.), the Pollution Control Department measured the air quality within a 3–4 km radius around the refinery—the same radial area—and confirmed that the measurement results are within normal standards," the statement added.
The company said it has also paused all production operations at the facility.
'PURE HELL' IN MOSCOW AS UKRAINIAN DRONES STRIKE MAJOR REFINERY SUPPLYING CAPITAL'S FUEL MARKET
Smoke and flames rise from the Bangchak oil refinery following an explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 26, 2026, in this screengrab taken from a video. (Nattawut Wonghirunkonchai/Handout via Reuters)
Local authorities issued a mobile phone alert to nearby residents around 3 p.m. local time advising them to avoid the area.
Officials later told residents they could return home but advised those living within 5 kilometers (3 miles) of the facility to be wary of air pollution.
CALIFORNIA OFFICIALS WARN MASSIVE CHEMICAL TANK WILL LIKELY SPILL THOUSANDS OF GALLONS OR 'BLOW UP'
Thailand's Pollution Control Department also said it was monitoring air and water pollution levels in the area.
Smoke rises from the Bangchak oil refinery following an explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 26, 2026. (Nattawut Wonghirunkonchai/Handout via Reuters)
The country's energy minister, Akanat Promphan, said the fire likely started at one of the refinery units, which is hundreds of feet away from where oil is stored.
OFFICIALS SAY POSSIBLE CRACK IN UNSTABLE CHEMICAL TANK MAY RELIEVE PRESSURE AT AEROSPACE PLANT
"If we’re not a hundred percent certain that the oil storage is safe, we won’t allow them to resume operations," Promphan said.

title: Egypt detains driver suspected of causing Cairo fuel tanker crash and inferno that left 31 dead
summary: The driver accused of sparking Cairo's deadly fuel tanker fire on the Ring Road is in custody as prosecutors detail the crash that led to the blaze.
story: Footage captures deadly inferno along Cairo's Ring Road on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, that left 31 people dead, officials said. (Credit: AP/UGC)

Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody.

The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared.
"It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock."
Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out."
STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION

Burned cars are seen as firefighters extinguish a fire involving a vehicle carrying fuel products on the Ring Road in Al-Warraq, Giza, near Cairo, Egypt, on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. (Mohammed Salah/AP)
Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames.
Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire.

They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. He then lost control of his car and veered far to the right while one of the fuel truck’s tires burst.
That caused the fuel tanker to hit the concrete wall of the highway and overturn, leading to the spill of fuel and the fire, according to the prosecutors' statement.
The stretch of the highway where the fuel tanker overturned is in Waraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area.
PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS
A fire burns where a vehicle carrying fuel products overturned and caught fire on a major highway in Cairo, Egypt, on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. (Habiba Abd El Aziz/Reuters)

On Thursday, commuters and pedestrians stopped to examine the scene. Black scorch marks covered the metal railings of one of the highway exits, where pedestrians and hundreds of vehicles had been trapped Wednesday night.
A high-voltage electricity line also lay twisted on the ground amid the black soot, while piles of ash lined parts of the Ring Road, according to the AP.

For hours after the fire, the injured were still arriving at nearby hospitals as families gathered outside them in a mix of shock and grief. Authorities said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to the scene.
Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record, the AP reported.
Bystanders gather next to the wreckage of a fuel truck in the aftermath of a fire in the Al-Waraq neighborhood near Cairo, on Nov. 25, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a massive multi-car pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Norse Atlantic airline suspends all flights, on brink of bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
summary: Norse Atlantic suspended all flights as its board warned it may file for bankruptcy without urgent short-term financing, leaving PIA passengers stranded.
story: Norse Atlantic, the Norway-based long-haul airliner, suspended all flights Thursday amid a liquidity crunch as jet fuel costs remain substantially higher than pre-Iran war levels. (Reuters)
Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights Thursday as its board warned the company may imminently file for bankruptcy if it can't secure short-term financing.
"If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy," the company said in a statement.
The airline, which provides long-haul flights between the U.S. and Europe, said it had been discussing with investors a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution."
SHIPPING GIANT WARNS STRAIT OF HORMUZ CHAOS IS 'NEW NORMAL' AS TEHRAN SHIFTS 4M BARRELS
But, the company added, "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found."
A Norse Atlantic Airways Boeing 787-9 aircraft is pushed back from a gate at Los Angeles International Airport in California on Aug. 10, 2022. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which contracts jets from Norse through a wet-lease program, shifted all United Kingdom flights to its own Boeing 777 planes, claiming Norse announced the suspension with no notice as PIA passengers were preparing to board.

Norse, amid rising fuel costs from the Iran war, began leasing out its Boeing 787 fleet to other airlines as it struggled to make a profit on trans-Atlantic flights. In July, IndiGo, India's largest carrier, announced it would conclude its own wet-lease program with Norse by the end of October.
An IndiGo Airlines aircraft prepares to land at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru on Dec. 4, 2025. (Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty Images)
Norse's stock price plummeted and closed down 85%. Most of its value has been wiped out since the start of the year and the stock is now trading at $0.010.

Jet fuel prices in Europe have more than doubled since March amid fallout from the Iran war and the restrictions on oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz, where up to 20% of the world's petroleum flowed before the onset of the war in February.
The price increases have forced other airlines, most notably budget carrier Spirit Airlines, to shut down as well.
DUFFY BLAMES BIDEN-BUTTIGIEG TEAM FOR SPIRIT AIRLINES COLLAPSE AFTER BLOCKED MERGER
"Long-haul, low-cost is most exposed to high fuel costs as demand is subject to a high level of price elasticity. So maybe not a surprise," aviation analyst James Halstead told Reuters.
Spirit Airlines jets sit on the tarmac at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport in Florida on May 2, 2026. (Giorgio Viera/AFP via Getty Images)
Norse Atlantic did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart' after judges question key charges
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared his corruption trial "fell apart" as judges urged prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases.
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized Zohran Mamdani over the NYC mayor’s call for his arrest as large anti-Israel protests descended upon the city during his address to the UN General Assembly.

The decade-long legal battle against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suffered a major blow Wednesday after judges cast doubt on key corruption charges, prompting the Israeli leader to declare that his trial had "fallen apart" and demand an immediate end to the proceedings.

A three-judge panel at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara consider dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu, questioned whether a criminal offense occurred in a second case and recommended resolving a third through a plea deal.
"Today, the trial fell apart," Netanyahu said in an evening address following the proceedings, according to The Times of Israel.
FROM INTELLIGENCE SHARING TO MISSILE DEFENSE, HOW ISRAEL'S PARTNERSHIP PROTECTS AMERICAN SECURITY
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu attends his trial on corruption charges at the district court in Tel Aviv March 12, 2025. (Yair Sagi/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
"Ten years ago, I said, ‘There will be nothing because there was nothing.’ But it took 10 years for this truth to be revealed to everyone," he said.
"Citizens of Israel, this trial must end immediately. And what also needs to end immediately is what came out of it — the hatred, the incitement, the division."
The court's intervention dealt a major setback to prosecutors more than six years after Netanyahu's trial began and roughly a decade after authorities launched the initial probe into him.
Judges had summoned Baharav-Miara to court Wednesday amid concerns over the strength of the prosecution's evidence and whether continuing the cases served the public interest.
"We’re now at a crossroad and need to rechart a new path," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told the attorney general, according to The New York Sun.
"Public interest dictates a need to rethink."
NETANYAHU REVEALS HE WANTS AMERICAN FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL TO 'DRAW DOWN TO ZERO'

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, center, waves from the stage next to his wife Sara during a Jewish New Year greetings event attended by Likud party members in Tel Aviv Sept. 17, 2026. (Jack Guez/AFPvia Getty Images)

She and her colleagues, Judges Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham, stressed that their comments were preliminary, did not constitute a verdict and applied only to Netanyahu because they still had to hear the other defendants’ testimony, The Jerusalem Post reported.
Baharav-Miara signaled that prosecutors would review the judges' recommendations and weigh their options.
Netanyahu faces charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust stemming from three corruption investigations.
Prosecutors announced the charges in November 2019 and formally filed the indictment in January 2020, and Netanyahu consistently denied wrongdoing.

The most serious charge, Case 4000, centers on allegations that Netanyahu granted regulatory favors to Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on the Walla news website, which was then controlled by businessman Shaul Elovitch.

Judges questioned whether prosecutors presented sufficient evidence to secure a conviction. In Case 2000, prosecutors also allege Netanyahu negotiated for favorable coverage from Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper publisher Arnon Mozes in exchange for legislation to weaken rival newspaper Israel Hayom.
TRUMP WANTS LARGEST-EVER ISRAELI HEAVY BOMB TRANSFER — BUT PROPOSAL HAS CONGRESS PREPARING FOR $2.8B FIGHT

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivers remarks during a toast by heads of Israel's political factions on the day of the inauguration of Israel's 26th parliament at the Knesset in Jerusalem Nov. 10, 2026. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
The proposed deal never materialized, and judges questioned whether a criminal offense had happened.
Case 1000 centers on allegations that Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, received almost $300,000 in gifts from Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan and Australian billionaire James Packer.
Judges suggested resolving that case through an agreement. Zion Amir, an attorney who previously represented Netanyahu in the proceedings, rejected the prospect of a settlement.
In his address Wednesday, Netanyahu also accused investigators of pressuring his political associates to testify against him and described the toll the investigations had taken on his family.
"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my wife and my sons," he said.
"Of delusional interrogations. Of character assassination. Of grave incitement that wounds the soul. Who will give us back those 10 years?"
Netanyahu, who requested a presidential pardon in November 2025 without admitting guilt, also called on his political opponents to set aside their differences and form a unity government.
"The boycotts must end, and now," Netanyahu said.

"I know what enormous and immediate dangers the State of Israel faces. There is only one way to deal with them. To unite in order to deal with them. We must unite to secure the future of Israel — no less than that, and immediately."
