title: Why Advent calendars are thriving in the ‘little treat’ economy
summary: Creators on TikTok and Instagram are helping to fuel the advent calendar craze, one review video at a time.
story: The countdown to Christmas began in October — at least on social media.

Over the past few months, content creators have been getting a head start on the holidays by unboxing, reviewing and promoting an array of Advent calendars. The anticipation behind each cardboard flap has translated into millions of views, as consumers lean into the surge in popularity surrounding the product.

“Brands are bringing out their advent calendars earlier and earlier, and so they go faster every year,” said TikTok creator Courtney Cahoon, who said nowadays she’s purchasing the calendars as early as August and sharing highlights with her 1.7 million followers.

The calendars originated in Germany in the 20th century, where a printer took inspiration from the candies attached to cardboard he had used to count down to Christmas as a child, according to retail giant Williams Sonoma.

While the calendars are not a new holiday offering, demand for the product has increased in recent years — which explains why it might feel like there’s a calendar for just about everything and for just about everyone. Global market for such calendars could reach $2.47 billion by 2033, according to trade publication Retail Insider.

Nowadays, the calendars have evolved into a marketing vehicle for brands looking to showcase everything from everyday essentials like McCormick’s spices to luxury goods like a $1,020 set of mini perfumes from Maison Francis Kurkdijan.
Experts like Freddy Tran Nager, an associate professor of communication at the University of Southern California, attribute the popularity of the calendars to what’s called “the treat economy.”

“We’ve had a rough few years,” said Nager, the founder of the marketing consultancy Atomic Tango LLC, referring to the economic challenges facing the U.S. economy. “And so you know, some people indulge in what’s called the ‘treat economy.’ They can’t afford a car. They can’t afford a home, but they can certainly afford little treats for themselves.”

Creators who specialize in sharing product recommendations on their feeds — sometimes in exchange for a commission from the brands — have also encouraged users to lean into indulging in calendar deals earlier and earlier.

On platforms like TikTok, searches for “advent calendar” spiked from Nov. 2-8, with the app reporting that many of its creators have posted videos sharing which calendars are underrated and which offer the best value. Ahead of Black Friday, TikTok said in a recent weekly trends report that more “creators are sharing holiday gift guides and reviewing advent calendars. Shoppers are also turning to TikTok Shop for holiday finds.”

Faire, an online wholesale platform that tracks consumer habits, told NBC News in an email that “by the end of September, retailers had already spent more on advent calendars than in all of last season.”
Hannah Wall, Faire’s trend expert, also attributed to the popularity of the advent calendar to “treat culture,” citing peak interest from Gen Z.

“Gen Z has made it an adult staple because it’s the ultimate small treat and they’re choosing squishies, tea, jam, and beauty countdowns over chocolate for a daily dose of holiday joy,” Wall wrote in an email statement.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Jintao Zhang, an assistant professor of marketing at Binghamton University, offered a similar observation.

“We know that the largest consumer group consuming social media is Gen Z,” he said, adding that the age group “determines the prevalence and also the attractiveness of advent calendar on social media.”

Social media users also tend to trust content creators, particularly those with smaller followings who are known as “micro” or “nano” influencers, according to Zhang. Still, he warned people to be cautious as some influencers post content that is sponsored without necessarily disclosing it in an obvious way.

Influencers typically approach their calendar videos in two different ways: Some do countdowns, going through each day of the calendar individually (as intended); while others open an entire calendar in one video, sharing its contents altogether.

Natalie Violette, a beauty and lifestyle influencer with more than 4 million followers on TikTok, said she either purchases or receives the calendars from brands in an effort to maintain authenticity in her reviews.

“They like seeing … the honest reactions and reviews on these calendars, and definitely … the surprise factor, no question, I think that’s what really brings them in,” said Violette, whose journey with this type of content began three years ago when a follower challenged her to do a complete makeup look just by using products from a calendar.
Her calendar videos have become so popular that they draw in new viewers every holiday season. The calendars she posts often sell out, she added.

Even calendars that she isn’t a fan of pick up traction online. For example, Violette was among the creators who criticized the Skims calendar, which, for $148, included hair ties and bobby pins. As a result of the online backlash, the Kim Kardashian-owned brand began offering refunds to customers who were unhappy with the product.

Sarah Lynn, who has built a following of more than 200,000 followers on TikTok for her calendar content, described it as “super fun” to show people what’s on the market. Sometimes, however, she said the offerings are hit or miss.
She particularly doesn’t appreciate when brands are “just filling it with random kinds of junk that they know are not really their best selling products.”

“If this was not my job and if this wasn’t what I was doing for work, I would not be spending all this money,” Lynn said. “But I never want people to feel like they have to buy anything or that they’re necessarily missing out.”
“Whatever people want to take from my content, they can definitely take from it,” she added. “Whether it’s entertainment or shopping inspiration or neither.”

title: Luka Dončić is a scoring machine. The NBA has rarely seen anything like it.
summary: Most NBA teams wouldn’t choose to let a player considered perhaps the greatest ever walk away in free agency.
story: Most NBA teams wouldn’t choose to let a player considered perhaps the greatest ever walk away in free agency. Yet that’s exactly what the Lakers did last summer — because most NBA teams will never have a franchise pivot ready to go quite like Los Angeles did.

Ever since Dallas stunningly traded Luka Dončić to the Lakers midway through the 2025 season and the Lakers paired the Slovenian superstar in his mid-20s with LeBron James, the all-time great who is a generation older, the NBA waited to see when the Lakers would decide to put the team’s future on Dončić’s timeline. That moment officially arrived last summer, when the 41-year-old James left in free agency and the Lakers didn’t try to stop the move.
There was no longer any doubt about which star the Lakers orbited. The only question was how comfortably Dončić would shoulder the championship expectations.

Nearly a fifth of the way through the regular season, the results have been extraordinary enough to push Dončić into a pantheon of scorers alongside such hallowed names as Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan — and thrust the Lakers into the discussion as a serious challenger to the Western Conference’s pre-ordained championship contenders, the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Only Chamberlain (in 1961 and 1962), Rick Barry (1966), Jordan (1986), James Harden (2019) and Elgin Baylor (1960) have scored more points through their first 16 games of a season than Dončić’s 586 thus far.

While facing Dončić during the last six years of his 14-year career, longtime NBA guard Reggie Jackson grew accustomed to his opponent’s tendencies and style, including feeling out a defense during the opening minutes. This season, “it’s kind of like he already knows all the answers,” Jackson told NBC News. “He comes out in the first quarter and he just he has his foot on the gas, and then from there, whether depending on what type of shot is going in, he kind of seems to play it off that.”

Dončić is scoring more than a point per minute and a league-high 36.6 points per game by taking and making more 3-pointers (4.8 on 13.2 attempts per game) and free throws (8.8 on 10.2 per game) than anyone. His accuracy both beyond the 3-point line and inside it exceed his career averages. Dončić has called it enjoyable to score as much, but has said he’s more driven by winning.

Iztok Franko, a data-driven Slovenian basketball analyst and author, has watched every game Dončić has played since he was a teenage sensation at Spain’s Real Madrid, and has seen Dončić produce a burst of high-scoring games before. Yet the combination of a hamstring injury that sidelined Dončić for both rounds of the Lakers’ postseason last spring and the team’s offseason decision to mold itself in his image had left Dončić “very motivated and hungry for this season,” Franko believes.

“Especially because this is now his team, with all the makeover the Lakers did over the summer. Luka had the longest period without basketball in his career, and the man truly loves playing basketball, so I think he had a huge itch to play, to entertain us again,” Franko said. “He also missed the Slovenian National Team play in the summer for the first time since 2017 and fully focused on rehab and preparing for this season.”

“So, I think all of that, plus the motivation for a good start, which was very important to avoid the noise, the criticism of the new team that would come if they would struggle out of the gate, contributed to him starting the way he did.”
Rob Pelinka, the Lakers’ president of basketball operations, compared Dončić to an illusionist, he told the team’s broadcaster this month, because “every night he does something unexpected.”

“If you look at the math or analytics of what he’s doing, it’s like in the same breath as Wilt Chamberlain. Like, did I just say that?” Pelinka said. “Like a modern-era player putting up those kind of numbers?”

After Dončić had scored 42 points to beat Miami eight games into the season, Heat star and two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo called Dončić “one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best.”
Did he meant currently playing, or ever?
“Of all time,” Antetokounmpo told reporters. “I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he’s got to be up there.”
That game was one of Doncic’s seven already with 40 points or more. No other player has scored 40-plus more than four times this season.

Any player scoring at a pace like that would face scrutiny over its sustainability, but with Dončić, such concerns are rooted in the reason why he is a Laker at all. When Dallas traded him in 2025 — after puzzlingly negotiating solely with the Lakers, without seeing what 28 other teams would offer — the Mavericks justified the decision partly by questioning Dončić’s commitment to conditioning.

Dončić responded last season with a much publicized and revamped offseason workout regimen, but on nights when his jumper was not falling, he could also depend on James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, and up-and-coming sidekick Austin Reaves to step up in his place.

Reaves is still a Laker, but with James gone the Lakers’ formula for success now hinges on Dončić to a degree rarely seen in NBA history. The NBA record for usage rate — a possession that ends in either a field goal attempt, a free throw attempt or a turnover by a certain player — is 41.6%, set by Russell Westbrook in 2017. Dončić is currently at 40.44%, by one measure, which if sustained would rank third all time.

Dončić touches the ball nearly 84 times per game, nearly 14 more than Reaves, the next closest teammate, according to league tracking data. The strategy has paid off; of the 43 high-usage players who touch the ball more than 60 times per game, Dončić’s points-per-touch average ranks third best.
“We live on a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light at all times when he’s on the court,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said.
A team hasn’t empowered Dončić to this degree since he led Dallas to the 2024 NBA Finals, said an NBA scout not authorized to speak publicly about player evaluations.

“I think the Lakers bought into the heliocentric style of play that the Mavericks tried to avoid at times” over concerns about his stamina, the scout said. “Credit to Luka for being in good enough shape to play that way the entire game.”
But, the scout added, “the test will be if he can withstand this level of play for 65-plus games.”

The Lakers have acknowledged the heavy burden. After Dončić scored 29 points on 28 field goal attempts during a loss to lowly Utah in November, Redick said that “the shot creation that is required from him takes its toll.” Perhaps as a result, his habits as a scorer have changed. Compared with his previous eight NBA seasons, Dončić is more reliant on 3-pointers, with 52% of his field goal attempts coming there and only 6% of his shots coming from within 3 feet of the rim, compared to his career rate of 15%.

Franko believes the biggest difference that has sparked this scoring run and the Lakers’ 15-3 record is “him being healthy and continuing with his commitment to off court, diet, training plan that started in the summer of 2025,” he said. “That, along with the motivation to lead this team, to prove this new team is capable of being better than people expect it to be, I think resulted in the biggest on-court change, which is his commitment to defensive end, and to play faster.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“I think defensively he was very good for [a] majority of the games, and his buy-in there has been crucial for Lakers success so far,” Franko added.

The Lakers’ commitment to Dončić as their leader was evident last summer, when teammates flew to Ljubljana, Slovenia, to spend several days training and hanging out with Dončić at his invitation. A Slovenian media outlet reported he had paid for his teammates’ chartered flight. The gesture was also symbolic: No other Laker is more responsible this season for whether the team can continue to fly high.

“It just feels like almost anything he shoots, whether it’s a circus shot, or whether it’s a regular stepback 3, or it’s a tough look, it seems like everything he shoots is going to go in,” Lakers teammate Quentin Grimes said in early November, after Dončić had scored at least 37 points in five consecutive games. “It’s kind of surreal. I don’t think I’ve ever been on the court when everything somebody shoots, you think it’s going in.”

title: Zelenskyy questions Trump’s ‘strange’ reference to Putin as a ‘friend’
summary: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration with the U.S. stance toward Russian leader Vladimir Putin, in the latest sign of deepening tension between Kyiv and Washington, as new questions emerged about Europe’s future financial commitments to Ukraine.
story: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration with the U.S. stance toward Russian leader Vladimir Putin, in the latest sign of deepening tension between Kyiv and Washington, as new questions emerged about Europe’s future financial commitments to Ukraine.

Zelenskyy said in an interview with the BBC broadcast Friday that he wants the U.S. to apply more pressure on Putin to stop his invasion of Ukraine, which began almost five years ago and grinds on despite President Donald Trump’s efforts to broker a peace deal.
The Ukrainian president described Trump calling Putin “my friend” at a recent summit in China as “strange” because the Russian leader is “an aggressor and a killer.”
“He can’t be a friend,” Zelenskyy told the British broadcaster in Kyiv, likening the statement to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment on Zelenskyy’s remarks. But Trump on Thursday defended his reference to Putin. “We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing,” he said.

“I could walk in and say, ‘I don’t like you!’ and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelenskyy and Putin,” he said. Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago, he added: “The biggest problem with that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other.”
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Zelenskyy was “insulting his counterpart,” showing that the Ukrainian leader “is not willing to follow the path of (a) peace settlement.”

The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Putin for war crimes, accusing him of personal responsibility for the abductions of children from Ukraine. The Trump administration has imposed sweeping sanctions on the court as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the U.S. and its allies, including Israel.
The Kremlin has said that Russia also does not recognize the ICC and considers its decisions “legally void.” Peskov in 2023 called the court’s move against Putin “outrageous and unacceptable.”

Zelenskyy’s comments were broadcast a day after Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy trying to mediate an end to the war, complimented Putin on being a “grandmaster” of politics and weeks after Kushner’s partner in peace efforts, Steve Witkoff, described Putin as a “humanitarian.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Moscow’s invasion has killed hundreds of thousands of troops and thousands of Ukrainian civilians. It also brought heavy sanctions on Russia and diplomatically isolated Putin in the West before Trump resumed relations.

At the same time, Zelenskyy has complained that the Pentagon is not delivering to Ukraine paid-for Patriot missiles that could stop Russia’s ballistic missiles and that SpaceX’s military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service, which is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communication, isn’t working properly.

Europe has in the past vowed to stay the course in helping Ukraine fend off Russia’s invasion. But European Union leaders on Thursday failed to reach consensus after fraught talks over a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year.
Elections in the EU over the next 12 months could amplify the influence of parties reluctant to send more money to Ukraine and may fray the continent’s support.
The grinding aerial bombardment between Russia and Ukraine has escalated recently.

Russia launched close to 300 aerial attacks a week through Nov. 20 on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, according to the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, or ACLED, which tracks violence.

title: Zohran Mamdani has successful surgery for torn Achilles and will make full recovery, staff says
summary: Surgery to repair New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Achilles tendon went well Friday and he’s now recovering at Gracie Mansion, his press secretary said.
story: Surgery to repair New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Achilles tendon went well Friday and he’s now recovering at Gracie Mansion, his press secretary said.
“The surgery was successful, and the Mayor is expected to make a full recovery,” the mayor’s press secretary, Joe Calvello, said Friday afternoon.
Mamdani underwent the procedure just after 11:30 a.m. and was done about 70 minutes later.

“He was discharged from the hospital and is now resting comfortably at Gracie Mansion,” the press secretary said. “We are extremely grateful for the first-class care the Mayor received from the medical staff today.”
First Deputy Mayor Dean Fuleihan is leading day-to-day operations today in Mamdani’s stead.
The first-term mayor tore his Achilles while playing a friendly soccer game between City Hall and the New York City press corps last week, during which he scored a goal.
He showed up to a news conference on Nov. 20 in crutches.
For Subscribers

“I forgot that I was 35, and soon after, I tore my Achilles,” Mamdani said at the time, noting he didn’t stretch before the game. “I will be in a boot for six to eight weeks. I will play soccer in about nine months.”
For Subscribers
During a Q&A following a news conference on Monday, the mayor said he admitted he was nervous about the procedure.
“I’m scared,” he said. “It’ll be my first surgery.”
Due to his recovery, Mamdani will miss the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, which was rescheduled to Saturday.

title: Princess Kate wants people to learn from her cancer journey in vulnerable new documentary
summary: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, reveals how cancer treatment terrified and changed her in a very personal documentary she said she hopes will help others reckon with the disease.
story: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, reveals how cancer treatment terrified and changed her in a very personal documentary she said she hopes will help others reckon with the disease.

In “Heal,” the royal reflects on mortality with an openness and vulnerability that pushes beyond the British monarchy’s once-trademark stoicism and reserve, describing the human challenges she faces after her treatment. The normally private princess gives viewers a glimpse — albeit a highly controlled one — of her cancer journey in the 30-minute film, which was produced to raise money for the Royal Marsden Hospital in London, where she received chemotherapy. The film marks a change in the way royals have spoken about their personal lives.

“William and Kate are communicating more directly with the public than ever before and being more open emotionally than we’ve ever seen,” said Emily Nash, NBC News’ royal contributor. “That really, I think, is as a result of her cancer diagnosis. It’s really changed their lives and they want to share what they’ve learned with the world.”

title: Thanksgiving shooting at Airbnb teen party ends with 1 dead, 6 wounded in Florida
summary: Gunfire erupted at a teen girl’s birthday bash in Florida on Thursday, leaving one dead and six others wounded after they showed up to the booze-filled celebration advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” officials said.
story: Gunfire erupted at a teen girl’s birthday bash in Florida on Thursday, leaving one dead and six others wounded after they showed up to the booze-filled celebration advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” officials said.
A 16-year-old “had her brother” or “another adult” rent a home via Airbnb in Davenport for a wild celebration that started late Wednesday night, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd told reporters.
“There’s no one person that should be accountable for this, but there’s an entire group of people that should be accountable,” Judd said.
A 15-year-old girl was shot in the chest and was initially listed in critical condition, though she’s expected to survive, Judd said.
Others wounded included a girl 16, two boys, 16 and 17, and two young men, 18 and 21.
The party was advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” according to the sheriff.

The birthday girl “is a juvenile. She’s a child,” Judd said. “So now we’ve got a juvenile renting an Airbnb. All of these folks are from Orlando, and as a result of that, we have this party that’s been advertised. And what does it say here? Get drunk, shots at the door.”
At its height, more than 50 people were at the party before 18-year-old victim and Orlando resident Oral “Glock” Walker Jr. pulled out his gun and opened fire first, Judd said.
That’s when another person at the party returned fire and killed Walker, Judd added.
The victim, who had a long criminal record, brought “a lot of cash and a lot of marijuana” to the party and might have been there to sell his product before the deadly dispute unfolded, Judd said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“He flashes his cash. He’s got his gun. He’s cool,” Judd said. “And for whatever reason ... he pulled the gun and started the gunfight and somebody smoked him like a Thanksgiving Day turkey.”
The birthday girl’s mother, 45-year-old Brianna Jacques, was arrested after officials alleged that she hindered the investigation.
“Mama shows up and instead of cooperating, [she] starts throwing a natural fit and screaming and hollering because we’re talking to her daughter, who is one of our potential witnesses,”  Judd said.
Jacques did not respond to a request for comment.
The sheriff blamed Airbnb and the home’s owner for the incident.

“Airbnb needs to have a lot of insurance. It appears to me clearly that they were negligent,” he said. “Airbnb, you probably need to lawyer up because I know a lot of parents that would be coming after y’all.”
A representative for Airbnb declined to name the homeowner who rented the house out for this party.

“We are heartbroken by this tragic gun violence, and our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone affected by it,” Airbnb said in a statement Friday. “Airbnb prohibits disruptive and unauthorized parties, and our Safety team has removed the individual who booked this stay in violation of those rules. Our law enforcement response team has contacted the Polk County Sheriff’s Office to offer our assistance in their investigation.”
The sheriff urged the person who gunned down Walker to contact investigators because there is a likelihood he could have been acting in self-defense.
“So show up and talk to us. You certainly have a right to defend yourself,” Judd said. “You shouldn’t have run, but you did. But it’s not too late.”

title: Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer’s husband died by suicide, spokesperson says
summary: The husband of Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., died by suicide, her office announced. Bruce Fischer made headlines for refusing to shake the hand of Kamala Harris in 2025.
story: The longtime husband of Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., died by suicide, her office announced on Friday, after initially saying that he “passed away peacefully” nearly a week ago.

Fischer first released a statement on X on Sunday announcing that her husband of more than 50 years, Bruce Fischer, died the day prior to the post “doing what he loved the most, spending time outdoors.”
Fischer, a Republican who has served in the Senate since 2012, wrote in the first statement that she would “cherish the decades we spent building a family in the Nebraska Sandhills.”
“Above all, Bruce was a loving husband, a devoted father and grandfather, a man of faith and a rancher,” the official wrote on Nov. 23.
On Friday morning, a spokesperson for the senator released a statement on a “sad update in the death” of Bruce Fischer.
“Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home,” the statement on X read. “Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life.”
For Subscribers
The spokesperson did not disclose details about the suicide or how the determination was made.
For Subscribers
Fischer has been in office since 2012 and is currently serving her third term. She and her husband were cattle ranchers and continued to run a ranching business, according to her official biography.

Bruce Fischer largely avoided the public spotlight, but made headlines in 2025 when — during his wife’s swearing-in ceremony — he appeared to decline the handshake of then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Black Friday shoppers head to brick-and-mortar stores across the U.S.
summary: The tradition of Black Friday bargain-hunting was alive and well this year as shoppers headed to malls around the country to scrounge for deals and revive an annual retail custom.
story: The tradition of Black Friday bargain-hunting was alive and well this year as shoppers headed to malls around the country to scrounge for deals and revive an annual retail custom.

Americans from coast to coast committed to the pre-Amazon memory of Thanksgiving weekend shopping, which lost steam in recent years as companies leaned into weekslong online sales and fewer early-morning doorbusters.

“We’re happy to see people back in the mall,” Arly Klein of Teaneck, New Jersey, told NBC News on Friday at the Westfield Garden State Plaza mall, where she looked for holiday presents for family, friends and co-workers.

“I feel like there were years, especially after Covid, where people weren’t really shopping in the stores,” Klein said. “We’re happy to, like, touch and feel and really like get the sense and feel the energy.”

Simeon Siegel, a consumer equity researcher at Guggenheim Securities, was at the Paramus, New Jersey, retail hub observing the Black Friday scene. It “feels like what Black Friday used to feel like” down to to the shortage of mall parking, the industry expert said.
“It’s fun again,” Siegel said. “People are coming to the mall not just because they feel like they need to — they feel like they want to.”
The analyst said lines, early sales and crowds are still part of the Black Friday routine but “stampedes” and other extreme aspects of the yearly ordeal seem to be phasing out.

The Citadel Outlets mall near Los Angeles was stirring with shoppers starting Thursday night, with lines forming around lit-up Christmas and palm trees outside storefronts, according to NBC Los Angeles.
There was a similar scene at the Dolphin Mall in Miami, where punctual customers were rewarded with a mystery gift card with prizes ranging from $10 to $500, NBC South Florida reported.
More shoppers were expected to to go to a physical store over the holiday weekend than at any point since 2019, according to a survey conducted by the ICSC, a commerce industry organization.

The association also reported that more than 75% of participants in Thanksgiving weekend shopping also planned to dine out and that more than 50% were expected to splurge on entertainment and activities.
Nearly 90% of adults in the U.S. planned to spend money over the holiday weekend, according to the survey.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
At a Boston-area shopping center, two women from England were on their 15th visit to the area for Thanksgiving and Black Friday.
“We love the bargains that we can get here,” Sue Holloway told NBC Boston from the South Shore Plaza in Braintree, Massachusetts. “We can’t get them at home.”
Holloway added that she and her traveling partner, Claire Caddy, “love to have a nice meal in the hotel and then we just shop, shop, shop.”
Caddy said shopping in person is far better than the online alternative.
“We like to come and see what we’re getting and choose for our family and friends,” Caddy said. “It’s not the same online.”

Molly Zocco, of Newington, Connecticut, was at the Westfarms Mall early on Friday to keep a family tradition going. Other early discount-seekers also said they were drawn to the shopping center because it was a cherished ritual.
“It’s definitely fun waking up early and going with my mom,” Zocco told NBC Connecticut.

summary: Amazon’s Black Friday sale is live now, and we gathered the top deals you won’t want to miss. Find sales on Apple, Dyson and more.

Some of the trendiest deals right now include the Apple AirPods Pro 3, Shark Depuffi and Medicube Zero Pore Pads. But don’t wait to shop: These deals won’t be around for long.

I’ve covered Black Friday and Cyber Monday as a commerce editor for NBC Selected for more than six years, so I know how to find deals that are actually worth buying. I spent weeks combing through thousands of discounts to find the best Black Friday deals on Amazon — each one I recommend below is highly rated and 20 percent off or more. When possible, I ran deals through price trackers to make sure they’re at their lowest price in at least three months or lowest price ever. I’ll frequently update this list throughout Black Friday.

Best Amazon Black Friday deals overall
Oura Ring 5

The latest iteration of the Oura Ring, which is currently at its lowest price ever, is slimmer than the previous versions, making it sleeker and much more discrete. The Oura Ring 5 tracks several health metrics, including heart rate, body temperature and respiratory rate, plus it automatically detects and logs exercise and sleep. The battery lasts up to nine days per charge (up from eight for the previous version). Keep in mind the ring requires an Oura membership subscription ($5.99 per month or $69.99 per year).
Apple AirPods Pro 3

A few months ago, I finally upgraded my earbuds to the Apple AirPods Pro 3 and have used them every day to listen to music and take calls. I love that they block out all noise when I want them to, and there’s no loud background sounds when I’m chatting on the phone. They also have built-in heart rate sensing, live language translation, hearing aid and hearing test features. They come with five sets of ear tips in different sizes and a charging case.
Stanley Quencher H2.0 Flow State 40-Ounce Tumbler

Our editors agree that the Stanley Quencher withstands the test of time. It keeps drinks cold and ice frozen for hours thanks to its stainless steel construction and double-walled vacuum insulation. The base is cup holder-friendly and you can move the lid to drink, place a straw or completely cover the top. The large handle also makes it comfortable to hold wherever you go.
We can help you find
Audible

If you’re an audiobook lover, Amazon is now offering three months of Audible Standard for less than $1 a month. You can purchase audiobooks outright, but subscribing to Audible Standard gets you access to one audiobook every month, unlimited podcasts and exclusive deals and sales. With the discount, you’ll also get a $20 Audible bonus that you can put toward eligible audiobook purchases. After the three months is up, your subscription will auto-renew at $8.99 per month (you can cancel at any time).
Apple AirTag

I add an AirTag to my luggage every time I travel to give me peace of mind. The trackers automatically connect to my iPhone and I can see their location on a map in the Find My app. When I need help finding something, the app gives me directions that lead me to it, and I can ring the AirTag so it plays a loud sound. It runs on a replaceable battery that lasts for over a year.
Ember Mug 3

With this self-heating mug, you’ll never have to microwave your lukewarm coffee again. I’ve been a fan of the Ember Mug since 2021, and after recently trying the brand’s latest release, the Ember Mug 3, I’m newly obsessed. The mug can warm beverages at temperatures up to 145 degrees Fahrenheit, which you can control using the buttons on the mug or via the Ember app. It can keep drinks warm for up to three hours in cordless mode, or all day when on the charging coaster. It’s also dishwasher-safe.
Hatch Restore 3

One of our favorite sunrise alarm clocks, the Hatch Restore 3 uses gradual light to gently wake you up in the morning, moving from red to orange to white before your alarm sounds. You can customize your sleep and wake up routine, play sound, adjust light and more using the companion Hatch Sleep app, or you can press the buttons directly on the device to control it. “I’m more likely to sleep through the night now since I’m not anticipating being startled awake by my phone’s blaring alarm,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin. You can use it as a bedside light to wind down, too.
Apple Watch SE 3

This smartwatch and fitness tracker compiles your health, sleep and workout data and syncs with your phone to mirror your apps and notifications. It has an always-on screen, fast charging and comes in two sizes (both of which are on sale).
Shark DePuffi

The viral Shark DePuffi has  a gua sha-inspired edge and six customizable temperatures that go from cold to hot. I use this device nearly every day and notice it makes me look so much less puffy and more awake in the morning . As you massage it along your face and neck, it depuffs, sculpts and temporarily relieves muscle tension. It comes with a charger and travel case, so you can take it on the go.
Crest 3D Whitestrips Professional Effects

One of our favorite at-home teeth-whitening products, this pack comes with 20 treatments that gently brighten your teeth over time and keep them white for at least 12 months, according to the brand. Crest recommends using the strips once a day for 30 minutes. The kit also comes with two one-hour express treatments you can use when you’ve got a bit more time.
Skylight Calendar

You can use this digital wall planner to color-code events, sync calendars across apps and add events via the Skylight app. You can also create a chore chart, custom lists, check the weather and more. NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman, who is a mom of two, uses this calendar to keep her family’s tasks and to-dos together. “Every family member gets assigned their own color, so at a glance you can tell whose dentist appointment is Tuesday and whose dance practice runs late on Thursday, without squinting at tiny text or scrolling through a shared app,” she says.
PicassoTiles 100-Piece Magnetic Tiles

These magnetic tiles are not only a great way to keep children entertained, but they can also unlock their creativity and help them understand color, geometrical shapes and architectural design. The tiles are scalable, so they can add more pieces to build as big as they want. Made for children three years and older, the tiles have smooth edges to avoid any cuts or bumps. This set comes with 100 magnetic tiles.
Dyson Airwrap i.d. Multi-Styler

You can use this Dyson Airwrap to dry, curl, straighten and more. It has three heat settings and six attachments for different hairstyles, plus you can pair it with the MyDyson App for even more customization options.
Life360 Tile Bluetooth Tracker (2 Pack)

You can attach these Tile Bluetooth trackers to your keys, wallet and more, so you can keep track of all your belongings. You can pair them with the Tile app to track their most recent location and ring the device if needed.
Nex Playground

This viral active play system that gets kids and families moving. It has a growing library of 60+ games from major brands, including Bluey, Fruit Ninja and Barbie. It connects to your TV and has a built-in camera to track motion and natural body movements. Plus, it supports up to four players at once (which varies by game), so the whole family can play together.
Medicube Toner Pads Zero Pore Pad 2.0

These TikTok-beloved toner pads are a favorite among our editors, who tested them for our Medicube brand guide. The pads are dual-sided: one side is textured to exfoliate, while the other is soft to hydrate and soothe your skin. NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown, who uses these pads to treat her hormonal acne, says the textured side feels gentle on her skin, so there’s no burning sensation during or after she uses it. They also come with a pair of small tongs, so you don’t have to use your fingers to separate the pads.
Samsonite Freeform 2-Piece Luggage Set

My Samsonite luggage stands the test of time; I’ve taken it around the world and despite getting beat up along the way, it still looks and feels nearly brand new. This set comes with one carry-on and one large checked suitcase, both of which have a hard outer shell. The bags are expandable, have interior organization systems like straps, pouches and dividers, and have TSA-approved locks and adjustable handles.
Lego Botanicals Succulents
These Lego succulents make for good desk decor or accent pieces in your home. The set includes nine tiny plants inside of terracotta-colored Lego plant pots.
UGG Women's Classic Micro Boot

Ugg’s Classic Micro shoes have a soft sheepskin inside that’ll keep your feet warm and comfortable during the colder months. They have the brand’s classic suede exterior and a tab on the back to make pulling them on easier.
Shark ChillPill

This portable fan came in handy during the hotter months, and I always carry it around in my purse or work tote in case I need a boost of cold air. It has 10 speeds, which is more than many other popular handheld fans I’ve tried, and a compartment for water that allows it to both function as a mister and activate the cooling plate on the side. I place the cooling plate directly on my neck to help lower my skin temperature on particularly hot days.
Energizer AA Batteries

If you’re looking to stock up on household essentials this Black Friday, this pack comes with 32 AA batteries. They can last up to 10 years in storage, which means you don’t have to worry about using them right away.
Best Amazon Black Friday home and kitchen deals
Cuisinart Glass Basket Air Fryer

This air fryer has a 4-quart clear glass, dishwasher-safe basket with a lid that let’s you monitor your food and store it away afterward. It has five functions — air fry, bake, broil, re-crisp, and keep warm — and you can adjust the temperature up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit.
Aura 10-Inch Digital HD Picture Frame

Upload your favorite photos and videos via the Aura app to display them on this Wi-Fi-enabled digital frame. The device will automatically swipe through the images when you walk by. The frame automatically adjusts screen brightness, crops photos, turns off automatically at night and has a built-in speaker for videos. You can invite loved ones to upload their memories, too.
Shark Upright Navigator Lift-Away Vacuum (NV356E)

Shark’s vacuum is one of our favorites for getting rid of dirt, crumbs, hair and dust due to its built-in HEPA filter. You can detach the pod to clean hard-to-reach areas like stairs and furniture, and it comes with two interchangeable attachments: a dusting brush and a crevice tool.
Fullstar Pro Original 4-in-1 Vegetable Chopper and Spiralizer

Slice, chop and dice vegetables using this dishwasher-safe kitchen gadget. The vegetable chopper has four interchangeable blades, including a small and large dicer, spiral blade and ribbon blade, all of which cut vegetables directly into an included collection tray.
Best Amazon Black Friday tech deals
Samsung The Frame 65-Inch Class Smart TV (2025 Model)

Samsung’s Frame Smart TV has a matte screen that makes it less reflective than traditional TV screens, and when it’s turned off, it becomes a digital frame that displays different artwork curated by the brand. You can also upload your own photos to add a personalized touch. (Ed’s note: This product slightly increased in price since Black Friday began, but because it’s 40% off and one of our favorite products, we think it’s a worthwhile deal.)
DJI Osmo Pocket 3 Creator Combo

The DJI Osmo Pocket 3 has a built-in stabilizer that keeps the focus steady as you shoot footage, plus a 2-inch touchscreen that you can rotate for both horizontal and vertical shooting. A single charge gives you more than 2.5 hours of battery life and the camera is so small and compact, you can vlog from anywhere. This bundle comes with a DJI mini mic transmitter to capture clear sound, plus accessories like mic windscreens, a mic charging dock and carrying pouch, a protective cover for the camera and a wrist strap.
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 16GB (2024 Model)

Amazon’s 2024 version of its Kindle Paperwhite has a 7-inch, glare-free screen and a thin, water-resistant design, so you can easily take your novels on the go (including to the beach or pool). The battery lasts up to 12 weeks on a single charge, plus you can adjust the display to read in either bright sunlight or in the dark.
Twelve South AirFly Pro 2

Place this Bluetooth transmitter into the headphone jack on an airplane seat, gaming console and more to stream audio to your wireless headphones. You can also plug it into a car’s AUX port to play music from your phone. The AirFly pairs with up to two headphones at a time, too.
JBL Charge 6

If you’re in the market for a new portable Bluetooth speaker, this one from JBL has up to 24 hours of playtime on a single charge and is water-resistant, so you can take it with you to the pool or beach. It also has a handle strap to make it easier to carry.
She’s Birdie 3.0 Personal Safety Alarm

This personal safety tool sounds a high-pitched siren and flashes strobe light when you pull the top ring, which helps draw attention when there’s a physical threat. You can attach it to your keys, phone or wallet, so it’s easily accessible while you walk, commute or travel.
Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro

Samsung’s Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, which were released earlier this year and are now at their lowest price ever, have comfortable rubber eartips and get up to seven hours of battery life, plus 30 more from the charging case. They also have noise cancellation and touch controls to easily manage playback, control volume, take calls and more.
Best Amazon Black Friday beauty deals
Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask

Biodance’s sheet masks have hyaluronic acid to hydrate and moisturize skin. I use these at least once a week and love how it goes from opaque to completely translucent overnight. My skin feels soft, smooth and hydrated as soon as I take it off in the morning.
COSRX Snail Mucin 96% Repairing Face Serum

This buzzy ingredient hydrates skin and targets fine lines, according to experts in our guide to snail mucin. This Cosrx serum, one of our favorite facial essences, is suitable for all skin types, lightweight and hypoallergenic, according to the brand.
Olaplex Wash & Shine Hair Kit

This Olaplex set comes with full sizes of the No.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo, the No.5 Bond Maintenance Conditioner and the No.7 Bonding Oil to hydrate, detangle and protect your hair from heat, according to the brand. Each product is suitable for all hair types.
Color Wow Dream Coat Supernatural Spray

“I have super frizzy hair and this product makes a noticeable difference while leaving my hair soft for days between washes,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. It prevents frizz and gives your hair a smooth finish after you style it. Plus, it doubles as a heat protectant to prevent damage.
Best Amazon Black Friday wellness and fitness deals
Liquid I.V. Sugar-Free Electrolyte Packets Classic Variety Pack

Mix this electrolyte powder with water to hydrate faster than drinking water alone, according to the brand. This variety pack comes with 16 packets in four sugar-free flavors: white peach, lemon lime, raspberry melon and green grape. Each pouch is also travel-friendly, so you can pour into any bottle while you’re on the go.
Nodpod Mineralized Silk Gentle Pressure Sleep Mask

The Nodpod is essentially a weighted blanket for your eyes. I have the original Nodpod and loved it so much that I got the silk version, which is much gentler on my sensitive skin. Plus, as a hot sleeper, I love that the silk feels cool. It’s machine-washable and doesn’t use straps, velcro or tension like most sleep masks, which makes it feel much less constricting.
Bala Bangles

Bala Bangles are one of our favorite wrist and ankle weights, and a popular option among our NBC Selected staff. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin loves using these weights in conjunction with her regular workouts and says they’re comfortable to wear and don’t slide around, even when she’s doing high-impact dance cardio and exercises like jumping jacks. They also lay flat and come with a travel pouch, so you can take them on the go. The weights come in 1 pound, 2 pounds and 3 pounds (all of which are on sale).
Therabody Theragun Mini (3rd Generation)

This massage gun is one of the most-used items in my house: I love to use it after long days at work and for recovery after a workout. It’s compact enough to take anywhere, and it has three massaging speeds and three head attachments to target different parts of your body.
Best Amazon Black Friday kids and family deals
Owlet Dream Sock Smart Baby Monitor

The Owlet Dream Sock is a popular wearable smart monitor that tracks your baby’s pulse rate, blood oxygen levels and sleep patterns in real time. Made for infants one to18 months old (six to 30 pounds), the Owlet will send alerts directly to your phone if your baby’s readings aren’t within the preset zones. The sock is made from comfortable fabric and wraps gently around your baby’s foot, plus it has up to 16 hours of battery life and connects via Bluetooth.
3Doodler Start+ Essentials 3D Pen Set

This 3D pen set has no hot parts, so it’s safe for children ages 6 and up to create 3D doodles, structures and more. The set comes with a doodle pad, 72 strands of mixed-color plastics, a USB-C cable and an activity guide to get them started.

Amazon’s 2026 Black Friday sale started on Thursday, Nov. 19 and runs for 12 days through Cyber Monday (Nov. 30).

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale ends on Monday, Nov. 30. Deals are available through the end of the event, but keep in mind that items might sell out and some offers (specifically Lightning Deals, which are on sale for only a short amount of time) can expire.
Unlike Prime Day, which is exclusive to Prime members, everyone can shop Amazon’s Black Friday sale. However, some individual promotions or benefits may only be available to Prime members.

Prime-exclusive deals, discounts on select subscriptions like Prime Video, and one- and two-hour delivery on fresh groceries from Whole Foods Market and Amazon Fresh.

title: Zohran Mamdani has successful surgery for torn Achilles and will make full recovery, staff says
summary: Surgery to repair New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Achilles tendon went well Friday and he’s now recovering at Gracie Mansion, his press secretary said.
story: Surgery to repair New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Achilles tendon went well Friday and he’s now recovering at Gracie Mansion, his press secretary said.
“The surgery was successful, and the Mayor is expected to make a full recovery,” the mayor’s press secretary, Joe Calvello, said Friday afternoon.
Mamdani underwent the procedure just after 11:30 a.m. and was done about 70 minutes later.

“He was discharged from the hospital and is now resting comfortably at Gracie Mansion,” the press secretary said. “We are extremely grateful for the first-class care the Mayor received from the medical staff today.”
First Deputy Mayor Dean Fuleihan is leading day-to-day operations today in Mamdani’s stead.
The first-term mayor tore his Achilles while playing a friendly soccer game between City Hall and the New York City press corps last week, during which he scored a goal.
He showed up to a news conference on Nov. 20 in crutches.
For Subscribers

“I forgot that I was 35, and soon after, I tore my Achilles,” Mamdani said at the time, noting he didn’t stretch before the game. “I will be in a boot for six to eight weeks. I will play soccer in about nine months.”
For Subscribers
During a Q&A following a news conference on Monday, the mayor said he admitted he was nervous about the procedure.
“I’m scared,” he said. “It’ll be my first surgery.”
Due to his recovery, Mamdani will miss the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, which was rescheduled to Saturday.

title: Hackers attack and penetrate Air Force’s computing platform
summary: Hackers penetrated the Air Force’s cloud computing platform in a breach that could have exposed sensitive military information, a U.S. official said Friday.
story: Hackers penetrated the Air Force’s cloud computing platform in a breach that could have exposed sensitive military information, a U.S. official said Friday.
The official confirmed the hack to NBC News but could not  provide any additional information about timing or the attack’s impact.
“The department of the Air Force does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities, or operational status of specific networks and systems,” an Air Force spokesperson said.
For Subscribers
Reuters first reported about this most recent cyberintrusion against federal assets.

The FBI’s National Crime Information Center — which is used by federal, state and local authorities to share important information — was recently breached, sources briefed on the matter told NBC News this week.
For Subscribers

And about two months ago, the FBI and Dutch national police arrested leaders of a “global cybercrime and threat actor group” that allegedly stole employee information from a bureau database. It is unclear whether any of these breaches are related.

“We continuously take prudent measures to protect department information, systems, and mission capabilities,” the Air Force spokesperson said Friday. “Ensuring the security, resilience, and availability of our most critical war fighting assets remains a top priority.”

“The department continues to assess and modernize its enterprise cloud capabilities to meet, evolving mission, security, resilience, and user requirements,” the statement continued. “Decisions regarding technical architecture, workload placement, contracts, and future capabilities are made through established governance, acquisition, and risk management processes.”

title: Thanksgiving shooting at Airbnb teen party ends with 1 dead, 6 wounded in Florida
summary: Gunfire erupted at a teen girl’s birthday bash in Florida on Thursday, leaving one dead and six others wounded after they showed up to the booze-filled celebration advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” officials said.
story: Gunfire erupted at a teen girl’s birthday bash in Florida on Thursday, leaving one dead and six others wounded after they showed up to the booze-filled celebration advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” officials said.
A 16-year-old “had her brother” or “another adult” rent a home via Airbnb in Davenport for a wild celebration that started late Wednesday night, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd told reporters.
“There’s no one person that should be accountable for this, but there’s an entire group of people that should be accountable,” Judd said.
A 15-year-old girl was shot in the chest and was initially listed in critical condition, though she’s expected to survive, Judd said.
Others wounded included a girl 16, two boys, 16 and 17, and two young men, 18 and 21.
The party was advertised as a “Girls Gone Wild Pajama Party,” according to the sheriff.

The birthday girl “is a juvenile. She’s a child,” Judd said. “So now we’ve got a juvenile renting an Airbnb. All of these folks are from Orlando, and as a result of that, we have this party that’s been advertised. And what does it say here? Get drunk, shots at the door.”
At its height, more than 50 people were at the party before 18-year-old victim and Orlando resident Oral “Glock” Walker Jr. pulled out his gun and opened fire first, Judd said.
That’s when another person at the party returned fire and killed Walker, Judd added.
The victim, who had a long criminal record, brought “a lot of cash and a lot of marijuana” to the party and might have been there to sell his product before the deadly dispute unfolded, Judd said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“He flashes his cash. He’s got his gun. He’s cool,” Judd said. “And for whatever reason ... he pulled the gun and started the gunfight and somebody smoked him like a Thanksgiving Day turkey.”
The birthday girl’s mother, 45-year-old Brianna Jacques, was arrested after officials alleged that she hindered the investigation.
“Mama shows up and instead of cooperating, [she] starts throwing a natural fit and screaming and hollering because we’re talking to her daughter, who is one of our potential witnesses,”  Judd said.
Jacques did not respond to a request for comment.
The sheriff blamed Airbnb and the home’s owner for the incident.

“Airbnb needs to have a lot of insurance. It appears to me clearly that they were negligent,” he said. “Airbnb, you probably need to lawyer up because I know a lot of parents that would be coming after y’all.”
A representative for Airbnb declined to name the homeowner who rented the house out for this party.

“We are heartbroken by this tragic gun violence, and our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone affected by it,” Airbnb said in a statement Friday. “Airbnb prohibits disruptive and unauthorized parties, and our Safety team has removed the individual who booked this stay in violation of those rules. Our law enforcement response team has contacted the Polk County Sheriff’s Office to offer our assistance in their investigation.”
The sheriff urged the person who gunned down Walker to contact investigators because there is a likelihood he could have been acting in self-defense.
“So show up and talk to us. You certainly have a right to defend yourself,” Judd said. “You shouldn’t have run, but you did. But it’s not too late.”

title: Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer’s husband died by suicide, spokesperson says
summary: The husband of Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., died by suicide, her office announced. Bruce Fischer made headlines for refusing to shake the hand of Kamala Harris in 2025.
story: The longtime husband of Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., died by suicide, her office announced on Friday, after initially saying that he “passed away peacefully” nearly a week ago.

Fischer first released a statement on X on Sunday announcing that her husband of more than 50 years, Bruce Fischer, died the day prior to the post “doing what he loved the most, spending time outdoors.”
Fischer, a Republican who has served in the Senate since 2012, wrote in the first statement that she would “cherish the decades we spent building a family in the Nebraska Sandhills.”
“Above all, Bruce was a loving husband, a devoted father and grandfather, a man of faith and a rancher,” the official wrote on Nov. 23.
On Friday morning, a spokesperson for the senator released a statement on a “sad update in the death” of Bruce Fischer.
“Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home,” the statement on X read. “Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life.”
For Subscribers
The spokesperson did not disclose details about the suicide or how the determination was made.
For Subscribers
Fischer has been in office since 2012 and is currently serving her third term. She and her husband were cattle ranchers and continued to run a ranching business, according to her official biography.

Bruce Fischer largely avoided the public spotlight, but made headlines in 2025 when — during his wife’s swearing-in ceremony — he appeared to decline the handshake of then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Skyler Gisondo Reveals This Actor ‘Never Breaks’ Character — Even On Set of ‘Focker-In-Law’
summary: Skyler Gisondo talks all things “Focker-In-Law,” including Ben Stiller’s fatherly advice and reuniting with the “Booksmart” cast.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions.
It’s pretty nice having Ben Stiller as a father. Just ask Skyler Gisondo. He’ll tell you that Stiller as a dad — even just an on-screen one — is nothing short of “inspiring.”

Stiller has played Gisondo’s dad not once, but twice now. First, in the 2014 movie “Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb,” and now as Greg Focker, a neurotic dad to his earnest-but-infantilized son, Henry, in the new movie “Focker-In-Law.”

Also starring Robert De Niro, Ariana Grande, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo, Owen Wilson, Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco, the fourth release in the “Meet the Parents” franchise captures the same feelings as the original: zany, uncomfortable and cringeworthy.

A newcomer to the series, Gisondo is also having a breakout moment in Hollywood with “Booksmart,” “Superman” and “The Righteous Gemstones.” He’s also set to star in “Man of Tomorrow” and “Shrek 5,” slated for summer 2027.

Gisondo dropped by the TODAY.com Lounge to dish on all things Focker — including working with “Ari” Grande — which co-star made him break character on the set and the fatherly advice Stiller gave him that wasn’t really advice at all.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

It was amazing. I mean, I grew up with these movies, like we all did, and just coming back to them again and again. So to get to step into this world and to be with these total heroes of mine, and icons, was just kind of a dream come true.

Fatherly advice? (Laughs). Well, it was more like the advice came in the form of just working together and really just kind of seeing the way that he did this job. He works so hard and he’s so methodical.

I remember there was a night where he had everybody over to his place and it was like obviously amazing. And I think he could tell I was just ... my head was spinning. I was like, “Wow, this was such a fun night.”

And he said something to the effect of like, “Keep working the way you’re working, keep doing it the right way and this is the way it’s headed for you,” kind of thing. And that was a very clear moment. Just very inspiring and really made me wanna keep going.
But, yeah, I learned really by his example of what it takes to do it at his level and how much he cares about the work.

We often didn’t. Eduardo’s the worst culprit because he breaks everybody a lot. And, also, once he breaks it, that breaks you because his laugh is like the most contagious. He cannot bottle it back up once it’s out, which only makes things worse.

But, yes, specifically that scene where Ben is serenading Bob, I mean, that’s a moment when you feel like you’re watching “Meet the Parents” in real time, and you’re forgetting that you’re in the movie. So that was tough.

But Ben never breaks. I remember actually being in “A Night at the Museum” and asking Ben, “How do you never break?” And was just like, “This is the job. This is what you do.” That really stuck with me, too, because oftentimes, when you want to break, it’s because it’s the best moment. And so it would be a real shame to mess it up, you know?
So, yes, you try, but ultimately you’re going to fail. Especially with those guys, you’re going to fail a lot.
But that day, I think, was tough for everybody.

It’s so special, too. I think that we all knew at the time what a special experience (“Booksmart”) was. And the further we get from “Booksmart,” it becomes even more clear to us just how special it was.

We were all in our early 20s. Olivia (Wilde), who we knew was such an extraordinary filmmaker then, and you see just the path that she’s been on, she just gave us so much room to run, and instilled so much confidence in us at a really important time in our lives and in our careers.

And so it is like a high school reunion. Eduardo and I, weirdly, have worked together like four times now. Beanie, that was our first time working together again. “From lovers to brother and sister,” we like to say. Weird pipeline, but that’s that’s the way it went down.

We all have so much fun together and there’s just so much love. We send a lot of selfies to Olivia whenever we’re together. And Ari is an honorary member — it felt like spiritually she was in the “Booksmart” group for sure.

title: Kate Middleton Details Being in the Hospital for Cancer Treatment in New Doc: ‘A Really Dark Time’
summary: Catherine, Princess of Wales, is revealing she endured “scary” and “dark” moments during her cancer treatment. The former Kate Middleton has a new documentary.
story: Catherine, Princess of Wales, is revealing she endured “scary” and “dark” moments during her cancer treatment, and the simple gesture that made her feel better, in her new documentary.
The British royal announced her diagnosis in 2024, without publicly sharing the type of cancer she was dealing with. The following year, she said she completed treatment and is now in remission.
In “Heal: A Princess of Wales Special,” the former Kate Middleton describes what it was like to be in a hospital and the comfort of having someone there to support her.

“When you’re on your hospital bed and it is so clinical around you — you haven’t got fresh air, no greenery around you. It’s very stark and alien and stripped back. The darkness was a really scary, disorientating experience. I think I was sort of in and out of consciousness. It was a really dark time,” she says in the documentary.

“But also then somewhere through that, too, when I became aware of someone holding my hand. They weren’t talking to me. They weren’t trying to fix anything. They were just there, and the presence of someone that stood by me in that time, I’ll forever be grateful for.

“It really made me realize the importance of simply being alongside somebody through their darkest times. So often you think you need to fix something or say something or do something, and you don’t. You just need to be there, and that’s what love looks like. That’s what I think the light is that we can often find out of the darkest of times.”
“Heal” premieres on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT. The documentary airs on Bravo at 11:30 p.m. ET/PT the same day and streams the following day on Peacock.
It’s a “deeply personal look” at the royal’s life after her cancer diagnosis and remission, according to a news release from NBCUniversal, the parent company of NBC, TODAY and Peacock.
TODAY former co-anchor Hoda Kotb, who is a breast cancer survivor, will give a special introduction.

The film includes footage of the princess and her younger brother, James, hiking the National Three Peaks Challenge in the UK, which involves summiting the three highest peaks of Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

title: After That ‘Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Finale, We Asked Malin Åkerman and Brittany Snow: Is It a Love Story?
summary: Malin Åkerman and Brittany Snow unpack Season 2 of “The Hunting Wives” in an interview.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions. In this edition, we spoke to “Hunting Wives” stars Brittany Snow and Malin Åkerman for a breakdown of Season 2.
Warning: This post contains light spoilers for “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 ending.
“The Hunting Wives” is back, and so are the wigs and the rifles.

The series became a phenomenon when it dropped on Netflix last year. The show didn’t shy away from steamy scenes between the titular hunting wives themselves, who are all residents of Maple Brook, a fictional gossipy town in East Texas. On top of that, there’s copious amounts of intrigue and murder (we’re talking lots of it).

Last season, Sophie (Brittany Snow), a transplant from the northeast, moved to Maple Brook with her husband and son. She developed an electric, forbidden connection with Margo (Malin Åkerman), a socialite and wife of an oil tycoon-turned-politician. Unable to pull away from Margo, Sophie found herself embroiled in her mess (and arms).

Without giving away too many spoilers, Season 2, out Nov. 26, shows viewers even more murder and mess. In it, a reality TV producer comes to town to create a show centered on the wives and their friends. Meanwhile, Margo and Sophie can’t stay away from each other, and can’t stay away from trouble.
The show has already been renewed for a third season. Below, Åkerman and Snow break down the charged dynamic at the heart of Season 2 and what it might mean for the episodes to come.

Malin Åkerman: “That is our big question too. I think that there are elements of love in this. I think that this is the closest to love that Margo’s ever gotten. But there are so many things that get in the way. I don’t know where this love story ends.”
Brittany Snow: “It’s a toxic, obsessed, real love story. It’s very real to them. It’s definitely not healthy. Are either one of them capable of true love? Probably not, with their backgrounds.”
Malin Åkerman: “I don’t think they don’t love themselves enough to know how to love someone else.”

Brittany Snow: “I don’t know if Margot is good for her necessarily, but I do think it’s good for her that she is finally living a truth that she’s shut away for a long time. Sophie is very much a caged bird in the first season, and in the second season, you really see that she’s not in a cage. If anything, she is completely unhinged, and I think Margo does bring that out in her. That’s a good thing. But I’m not sure it’s a healthy thing.”
Malin Åkerman: “Yeah, the murder part and the drinking part.”
Brittany Snow: “But it’s giving her more identity than she’s ever had in her marriage.”

Malin Åkerman: “If they’re going to pursue this love, then a happy ending would be them free, somewhere they can escape. They need to be obviously outside of America, where they can change their identities and just live together forever in some beautiful shack — Margo won’t just live in a shack anywhere. But, you know, somewhere where no one can reach them for the rest of their lives. They’ve done too much to go back. They’re both murderous, toxic people.”
Brittany Snow: “They’re going to end up with a lot of money and enjoy this new life, hopefully together, without killing each other.”

Brittany Snow: “I think it’s a little bit influenced by Margo. I think she’s so obsessed with Margo that she actually believes that’s what she also likes. In the third season — it’s sort of alluded to in the end of the second season — that she has all this money, but she’s a new type of Sophie. She’s a new woman, and how she dresses is indicative of that. But I think that scene specifically is for shock value too.”

Malin Åkerman: “The bikers are gone, so that’s good. I feel like Sophie’s always the biggest threat for Margo, just because she’s so smart, I think she can outsmart many people. She’s kind of that person that she wants on her side more than anyone. But everybody is an enemy at this f----- point. Callie’s out to get her. Jed’s out to get. She’s being hunted.”

Malin Åkerman: “She’s protecting Sophie from going to jail. She realizes in the car ride that Jed is literally going to make sure that Sophie goes to jail. The only way to keep Sophie out of jail is to team up with Jed and be on his side. It’s the one time that Margo acts selflessly, and Sophie doesn’t believe her.
Brittany Snow: “Why would I believe you?”
Malin Åkerman: “She’s cried wolf too many times. But think that’s the one time that she’s actually truthfully doing this.”

Malin Åkerman: “She is different from all the rest of them because she’s smart. She’s emotionally intelligent. She just comes in at another level. If you look around the town where Margo spent most of her years, there just isn’t that level of intelligence that comes from Sophie. I think that she’s intrigued by Sophie. She’s titillated by her brain. That’s new for Margo. The rest has been everyone’s her toy and it’s easy and she can be Lady Macbeth pulling the strings. Whereas with Sophie, it’s just a little bit more of a challenge, and I think she likes it.”
Malin Åkerman: “That’s a really good question. So much.”
Brittany Snow: “Sophie wouldn’t have gotten into this mess if she was true to herself. She wouldn’t have twisted up herself. Maybe Abby Jackson would still be alive.”
Malin Åkerman: “Well, I don’t know. Margo had a mess to clean up before Sophie got there.”
Brittany Snow: “But do you think the party would’ve happened?”
Malin Åkerman: “Abby still would’ve found out Margo was having an affair with her boyfriend. Margo doesn’t know how to diplomatically solve problems so she might’ve killed her.”
Brittany Snow: “But Sophie wouldn’t have been involved.”
Malin Åkerman: “Sophie wouldn’t have been involved. That’s good for Sophie. Margo’s f---- no matter what.”

title: I’m a Divorce Lawyer Who Watched ‘War.’ Here’s Who Really Came Out on Top
summary: Divorce lawyer Hannah Hembree Bell reacts to the “War” finale and says who came out on top and who won in the end.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a divorce lawyer breaks down the “War” finale.
Hannah Hembree Bell couldn’t turn her brain off while watching “War.”

A divorce lawyer and owner of her own Texas family law firm, Bell guides clients through situations resembling the characters’. In her assessment, the two leads were “awesome” — but the “legal part (of the show) was patently ridiculous.”
“War” follows a billionaire tech founder (Dominic West) and a Hollywood actor’s high-profile, high-net-worth split, and all the legal wheelings and dealings that ensue.

While watching, she was struck by how differently she would have advised Morgan and Carla than their own legal advisors. The lawyers brazenly blew past any attempt at a settlement, and employed shocking (and illegal) tactics like placing a mole in the other firm’s team.

“The lawyers inflamed the conflict. That’s why you have to be really careful in picking your lawyers. Are you picking lawyers who have big egos? Are they known to be willing to burn everything down, including your life?” she says.
Still, as over-the-top as the antics were, the “War” finale, which aired on Nov. 18, offered up a lesson or two for anyone going through a divorce.
What Happens at the End of ‘War’, and Who Wins?
After all that — and there is a lot of “that” — Carla and Morgan come to a reasonable settlement, bypassing the lawyers’ interventions.
They agree for Morgan to give Carla 50 percent of shares and monthly payments until he retires. They also have joint access to Carla’s son Gabriel (Aran Murphy), who Morgan helped raise.
Rather than Carla vs. Morgan, the show ended up becoming Carla and Morgan vs. their lawyers, and their lawyers’ scorched earth tactics.
“Ultimately, the winners are Carla, Morgan and Gabe because they came to terms that was best for their family given their unique situations,” Bell says.
The Advice She Would’ve Given Carla and Morgan
At the start of the divorce process, Bell advises her clients to dream up their best-case scenario.
Then, during each step, she has her clients ask themselves, “Will this action get me closer to or farther away from where I’m trying to go?”
Bell says most of the show would have been avoided if Morgan and Carla had taken that advice. “They would have just had a coffee and worked out the deal,” she says.

Morgan, for example, would have wanted a relationship with Carla’s son Gabe and control over Zephyr, his business. Carla would have wanted a good relationship with Gabe, too, and compensation for the work she did for building Zephyr.

“Then I would have said, ‘OK, if that’s the goal, and especially the Gabe part, we’re not going to go serving people at their movie premiere. We’re not going to go setting honey pots. That does not advance your interest,” she says.
“But if they’re not clear on what their interests are and what the outcome they want is, then they can take actions that thwart their plan.”
The 2 Lessons ‘War’ Offers About Divorce
“War” offers up other cautionary tales, including what happens when people act emotionally. Bell advises her clients to “do nothing when activated.”
“Whether you’re super happy, super sad, super mad, wait until that emotion passes before you act or do anything,” she says.
Her other recommendation is to “keep a tether to the person you’re divorcing, if it’s at all possible” — though, of course, sometimes it’s not.

Caught up in the drama and defensive measures, Carla and Morgan lost their connection to each other. But it got reestablished when Morgan’s love letter was read in open court, and they landed on a fair deal.
“If they had kept that connection, even if it was strained, I think they could have gotten there a lot sooner,” she says.

title: Could the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026 Be Canceled? Macy’s Shares Statement
summary: Heavy rain and wind is expected for Thanksgiving Day. Here’s what that could mean for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City.
story: Snoopy, Bluey and SpongeBob will still make their appearance in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade — just a bit later than expected.

Heavy rain and high winds are predicted in the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day, which raised the question of whether the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City would be grounded or canceled.
In a statement shared on Nov. 25, Macy’s confirmed it would be postponing the parade to Saturday, Nov. 28.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28. Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday,” the statement read.

The parade is broadcast live on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo. NBC also issued a statement: “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28. More details to follow. In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.”
A record-setting 100 balloons were set to float down the streets of Manhattan on Thursday, hosted by TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie, Al Roker and Hoda Kotb.
Here’s what to know as far as the forecast and change to the parade schedule.
Weather Forecast for Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade 2027

Heavy rain and wind gusts of 50-60 miles per hour, with the strongest winds from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., are forecast for New York City on Thanksgiving, according to NYC Emergency Management. There is a high wind watch for the New York City metro area from 10 a.m. Thursday to 1 a.m. Friday.
About 1-2 inches of rain, up to 2.75 inches, are also expected, with some flash flooding and possible thunderstorms.
“In the 32 years I’ve been doing the parade, I’ve never seen a forecast like this,” weatherman Al Roker said on TODAY on Nov. 25.
New York City regulations stipulate the balloons must be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 miles per hour and gusts exceed 34 miles per hour.

Those regulations were put in place in 1998 after severe weather at the previous year’s parade, which had wind gusts up to 43 mph. The wind sent a Dr. Seuss Cat in the Hat balloon careening into a lamppost on 72nd Street and Central Park West, snapping off a metal arm and injuring four people.
NYPD officers also had to ground and deflate the Barney and Pink Panther balloons, according to The Weather Channel.
As a result, the parade will take place on Saturday, Nov. 28.
What Happens in Bad Weather?
There has only been one edition of the parade where there were no inflatables flying. Fierce winds and rain prompted parade organizers to ground all the balloons at the 1971 event.
The NYPD and parade organizers can adjust how high the balloons are flying instead of grounding them entirely in the case of windy conditions.
At the 2019 parade, wind gusts went right up to the edge of the limit, reaching 33 mph. Vehicles were anchored to the balloons to fly them lower down Sixth Avenue in Manhattan.

Otherwise, the show has typically gone on despite the conditions. In 1989, 4.4 inches of snow fell by noon in the snowiest parade on record, according to The Weather Channel. In 2006, parade-goers endured nearly two inches of rain.
