The hackers shared leaked data with a number of other exiled Russian media outlets and the BBC, who all arrived at a figure close to the 490,000 reported by Mediazona. A similar estimate of half a million Russian troops killed was also shared by a senior British defense official in September.

Before the new analysis of the data in the Rosstat leak, the verified named list of Russia’s war dead compiled by Mediazona and the BBC stood at just over 289,000. It was based on obituaries, local news and official registries, and was the only publicly available database containing the fallen soldiers’ names.
The Russian Defense Ministry has not officially updated its death toll in Ukraine since the early months of the war, when then-Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu said it stood at nearly 6,000.

Mediazona warned that due to a considerable lag in military death registrations, Rosstat may not yet have finished capturing deaths from 2025. “That means the leaked records through late September — however authentic and reliable they are — still fall short of the true death toll,” it said.

title: Princess Kate wants people to learn from her cancer journey in vulnerable new documentary
summary: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, reveals how cancer treatment terrified and changed her in a very personal documentary she said she hopes will help others reckon with the disease.
story: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, reveals how cancer treatment terrified and changed her in a very personal documentary she said she hopes will help others reckon with the disease.

In “Heal,” the royal reflects on mortality with an openness and vulnerability that pushes beyond the British monarchy’s once-trademark stoicism and reserve, describing the human challenges she faces after her treatment. The normally private princess gives viewers a glimpse — albeit a highly controlled one — of her cancer journey in the 30-minute film, which was produced to raise money for the Royal Marsden Hospital in London, where she received chemotherapy. The film marks a change in the way royals have spoken about their personal lives.

“William and Kate are communicating more directly with the public than ever before and being more open emotionally than we’ve ever seen,” said Emily Nash, NBC News’ royal contributor. “That really, I think, is as a result of her cancer diagnosis. It’s really changed their lives and they want to share what they’ve learned with the world.”

title: A rising political star in China is the latest victim of Xi’s purge
summary: He was on the rise among China’s political elite, hosting tech leaders and senior American officials.
story: He was on the rise among China’s political elite, hosting tech leaders and senior American officials. But now Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a member of the country’s influential politburo, appears to be the latest senior official brought down by President Xi Jinping’s sweeping purge.

The hammer unexpectedly came down on Chen in the form of a two-line bulletin on the Xinhua news agency Tuesday: He is “suspected of serious violations of Party discipline and law and is currently under disciplinary review and supervisory investigation” — a common euphemism for corruption crackdowns on ruling Communist Party officials under Xi.
Public announcements such as these usually mark the end of a political career in China. Chen has made no public statement.

He is the fourth politburo member to be purged in less than two years, part of a broader crackdown that has swept aside top military leaders as Xi consolidates power. He is set to extend his rule next year, at a party congress that is held once every five years and looms over the preceding months.
But Chen’s abrupt downfall took many close observers of China by surprise, given his profile and career path would usually point to a bright future.

“He was potentially going to the highest level, which would be the standing committee. And I think from a lot of Western observers, people thought he had even better prospects,” Damien Ma, the Singapore-based director of the Carnegie China think tank, told NBC News.
Xi’s pursuit of loyalty

Some analysts have speculated that Xi, increasingly viewed as likely to rule for life, may have been purging a viable replacement. Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London, said however that Chen was “someone who could rise further but not as a successor.”

Chen, a 62-year-old technocrat known as a friend of foreign business and an advocate for AI, was an environmental scientist who studied in London and swiftly rose through the party’s ranks. He served as China’s environmental minister, Beijing’s mayor and the party secretary in Shanghai — a post once held by Xi and widely considered a stepping stone to bigger things.

Just last month, Chen hosted Apple Chairman Tim Cook, welcoming the U.S. tech giant to “make full use of Shanghai’s strengths” and bring more products to the city, a financial and cultural hub that has long served as a connection between China and the international community.
In his last public appearance last week, during a tour of a shipping facility, Chen called for advancing the industry’s digital transformation.
By Wednesday, Chen’s name has been removed from some official websites. A webpage on the Shanghai government site showing that meeting with Cook is now showing a 404 message, or not found.

Chen is just the latest senior official in the crosshairs of Xi’s long-running anti-corruption campaign and emphasis on party discipline, which analysts say is as much about loyalty as it is about reform.

“It is a warning to all technocrats, as Chen was a rising star among technocrats and had no apparent failures in a technocratic way. So, message is: adhere to strict party discipline and demonstrate unquestionable loyalty to Xi or else,” Tsang said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The party’s Central Committee, which has about 200 mostly male leaders, vowed to “ensure more rigorous discipline enforcement, and make full use of discipline as a guide, restraint, guarantee, and incentive” at its closed-door gathering, the fifth plenum, last month.

“What they’ve been building as part of this discipline machine over the last 15 years is to kind of implement their sort of internal operating system of how they deal with, let’s say, bad eggs within the party,” Ma, of Carnegie China, said.

“The top leadership is normalizing this anti-corruption, this self-cleansing,” Ma said. “It is now a normal part of what the party expects, and they’re trying to embed that over time and down to every single level,” he added.

The Chinese government has not announced any charges against Chen, who was the youngest member of the country’s elite decision-making body. The 24-member Politburo was unveiled in 2022 but is now down to 21 members after the purges. Last month, top general Zhang Shengmin was elevated to the body in a rare addition.

Chen’s undoing comes a year before the party’s top leadership is reshuffled at the 21st Communist Party Congress, when Xi is expected to solidify control even further and cement another five-year term at the helm of the country.
From London to Shanghai

Born in 1964, Chen studied at the prestigious Tsinghua university, long a major pipeline for senior party officials and where he served as president from 2012 to 2015. His name has now been removed from Tsinghua’s online list of former presidents.
After studying at Tsinghua in the 1980s, he moved for a decade to Britain, where he obtained a doctorate from Imperial College London in 1993.
Chen returned to Tsinghua’s environmental science and engineering department in 1998 before being named the university’s president in 2012, according to an official biography.
He’s authored dozens of papers, including on carbon emission reduction and water quality monitoring.

The relatively young Chen would ride around campus on his bike and built a reputation for pushing institutional reforms in his three years at the helm of the university, according to an article in People’s Digest, a magazine affiliated with the People’s Daily, the community party’s official newspaper.

The article, titled “From University President to Cabinet Minister,” was published in 2015, the same year he was picked to lead the Environmental Protection Ministry. In 2017, Chen became mayor of the capital, Beijing, where he oversaw the 2022 Winter Olympics during the Covid pandemic.

title: 2 men charged with burglary after break-in at Prince William and Princess Kate’s country home
summary: Two men have been charged in connection with a burglary at the Sandringham estate, police said, after a reported break-in at the home of Prince William and Kate.
story: LONDON — Two men have been charged in connection with a burglary at the royal family’s Sandringham estate, British police said Wednesday, after a reported break-in at the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate.
The pair were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site, the local police force said in a statement.

Officers were called just before 6 p.m. local time (1 p.m. ET) on Monday “to reports of suspicious activity at a property,” Norfolk Constabulary said. “Police and specialist resources attended and two men were arrested nearby on suspicion of burglary and trespass and taken into custody for questioning,” the statement added.
The two men, named by police as Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, have now been charged.

The pair were remanded in custody after a brief court appearance in the eastern city of Norwich on Wednesday morning, according to Britain’s Press Association news agency. Describing the accused as Albanian nationals, the agency reported that they were accused of stealing six pairs of cuff links and a clock, value unknown.

David Harrison, the games and conservation manager at the Sandringham Estate, told the court he was conducting a patrol when he saw two males jump through a hedgerow and run into a wooded area using a thermal spotter, according to the PA. He said he followed in a utility motor vehicle but could not locate the men.
The property, gifted to the heir to the British throne and his wife by the late Queen Elizabeth II as a wedding present, is nestled in the heart of the royals’ sprawling estate.
In an earlier statement, police said the property which has its own private swimming pool, a full-size, artificial grass tennis court and vast grounds, was unoccupied at the time of the incident.
Separately, a royal source told NBC News that the couple and their three children, George, Charlotte and Louis, were not there at the time.
The couple and their children have often enjoyed weekend breaks and holidays at the royal estate in eastern England.
While they weren’t present at the time of the burglary, the incident is a significant security breach for the royals.
The break in “of course, raises huge concerns,” NBC News royal contributor Emily Nash said Wednesday. “This is the home of our future king and queen.”
“Nobody wants to feel as though their home, their private space is being violated,” she said. “They do have a great deal of security in place and so they’ll be looking at why that has lapsed.”
Security arrangements “are naturally cloaked in secrecy because they don’t want to let people know too much about what’s happening,” she added.

“Essentially, it’s a bit like an onion. They have multiple layers of security,” she said, adding that when they were on the estate “they also have their armed police protection officers who ensure that nobody can get close to them.”

Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country house built in the early 1800s, entered the royals’ extensive property portfolio when it was bought in 1898 by Queen Victoria’s son, who would later become King Edward VII.

The prince and princess of Wales’ main home is Forest Lodge in Windsor, a small town around 30 miles west of London. The couple said they moved there for a “fresh start” in 2025 after the death of the late queen and Kate’s cancer diagnosis.
There have been several previous high profile security breaches involving the royal family.
In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. King Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at the property at the time.

But perhaps the most famous break in came in 1982, when a man called Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes talking with the intruder before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.
The latest incursion came days before the release of a new documentary about Kate’s cancer diagnosis and remission, called “Heal.”
Set to air on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from Dec. 1., the highly personal film will see her share her private thoughts on her illness and recovery.
“It changes your body, it changes you physically, but there is a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” Kate says in a clip released ahead of Sunday’s air date
“It is often through pain that we realize there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that,” she adds.

title: Nearly 6 decades after teen was killed while leaving job, Canada authorities know who did it
summary: Authorities in Canada have identified a man accused of killing a Canadian teen nearly six decades ago, police said Monday.
story: Authorities in Canada have identified a man accused of killing a Canadian teen nearly six decades ago, police said Monday.
Michael Joseph Moore, who died in 2018, was responsible for the 1968 death of Jacqueline “Jacky” Dunleavy, 16, according to the London Police Service in Ontario.

Moore, who worked as a firefighter for nearly three decades, was identified through genetic genealogy, officials said at a news conference Monday. The forensic technique combines modern DNA analysis with traditional genealogical research.
If Moore was alive today, the agency said in a statement, he would have been arrested and charged in connection with the teen’s death.
“Publicly identifying Moore provides an accurate historical record and answers that Jackie’s family and the community have sought for decades,” the agency said.
In a statement read at the news conference, Dunleavy’s family thanked law enforcement and said they hope the techniques used to solve her death can be used with other cold cases.
Authorities did not identify a possible motive, and a possible connection between Moore and Dunleavy remained unclear.

The high school sophomore was last seen on the evening of Jan. 9, 1968, leaving her job at a variety store in London, roughly 120 miles northeast of Detroit. Dunleavy was found dead at a school 90 minutes later, the police service said.
She had a head injury, according to the authorities, and her cause of death was determined to be strangulation.

Despite what the agency described as an extensive investigation, the case remained unsolved, and efforts in the decades that followed did not reveal her killer.

“The investigators who worked on Jackie’s homicide in 1968 did everything they could with the investigative and forensic tools available to them at the time,” Det. Sgt. Micah Bourdeau of the London Police Service said in a statement. “The evidence they carefully collected and preserved ultimately allowed investigators decades later to continue that work.”
Recently, a Texas-based DNA lab conducted specialized testing using that evidence and investigators were able to develop a family tree that helped identify Moore, the police service said.
After conducting additional interviews, gathering new evidence and obtaining comparison DNA samples, Moore was identified as the man responsible for the teen’s killing, the agency said.

Moore, who was 25 at the time, had moved to Canada from Ireland in 1967, authorities said. He worked as a firefighter for 28 years but did not have that job until after Dunleavy’s death, Det. Mike Budzyn of the London Police Service told reporters.
At the time he retired, Moore was a captain.
His family was shocked by the revelation, Budzyn said, and “expressed their hope that these findings will provide long-awaited answers for Jackie’s family.”

title: Two arrested over suspected burglary at royal family’s Sandringham estate
summary: Prince William and Princess Kate’s country home Anmer Hall has been broken into, police said. The Prince and Princess of Wales were not home, a source said.
story: LONDON — Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the royal family’s Sandringham estate, British police said Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate.

Police responded to reports of “suspicious activity” at the address Monday evening, dispatching searches by police dogs, drones a helicopter. That resulted in two men being arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing, according to a statement from the Norfolk Constabulary, the local police authority. The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident, it added.

The Sun newspaper first reported that police were investigating a break-in at Anmer Hall, one of the residences used by the heir to the British throne and his wife, nestled in the heart of the royals’ sprawling estate.

Kensington Palace, which handles communications for William and Kate, said it would not comment publicly on security matters. A royal source told NBC News that the couple and their three children, George, Charlotte and Louis, were not there at the time.
The Waleses’ main home is Forest Lodge in Windsor, where they moved for a “fresh start” in 2025 after the death of Queen Elizabeth II and Kate’s cancer diagnosis.

Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country house built in the early 1800s, entered the royals’ extensive property portfolio when it was bought in 1898 by Queen Victoria’s son, who would later become King Edward VII.
It has been used by various royals over the years. And William and Kate often enjoy the residence for weekend breaks and holidays.
The incident will sharpen an ongoing debate about royal security.
William, as a “working royal,” receives 24-hour armed security. But his brother, Prince Harry, does not, having moved to California in 2020 and relinquished his regal duties.

Harry is in a protracted battle with authorities in a bid to reinstate this arrangement, which he argues is necessary due to his high-profile position and history of serving in the armed forces in Afghanistan.
This summer, Harry and his wife, Meghan, and their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, moved back to Britain.

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. King Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at Windsor Castle at the time.

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

Hours after the break-in, William was meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday on the doorstep of No. 10 Downing St., where they are expected to discuss issues such as homelessness.
Meanwhile Kate is set to feature in a 30-minute documentary, “Heal,” about her cancer diagnosis and remission. It will air on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from Dec. 1.

title: Crowd evacuated from American rapper Don Toliver’s concert after ‘unknown substance’ released
summary: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
story: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
About 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated by emergency workers just after 10 p.m. local time (5 p.m. ET) from Toliver’s show at the Co-op Live venue in the northern English city of Manchester.
The North West Ambulance Service declared a major incident and​ said the substance was “believed to ​be tear gas” and was understood to ⁠have been released toward the ​end of the show.

“We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene,” it said in a statement, adding that one person had been hospitalized.
“More than 80 people were assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination was carried out as a precaution,” the ambulance service said Monday.

People in the crowd were suffering effects “from an unknown substance,” Greater Manchester police said in its latest statement Monday. “Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident,” police added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The venue, in the center of the busy city, was hosting Grammy Award-nominated R&B rapper-singer Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, as part of his Nitrous tour.
The Houston-based rapper is best known for hits “No idea” and “After Party,” and features on the soundtrack to the new “Grand Theft Auto VI” blockbuster game.

In a statement posted to Instagram, Toliver said he was “very sad” to announce that he would have to cancel his London show on Monday “due to the incident in Manchester” and would instead perform on Dec. 15.
“I Just Wanna Make Sure Everyone is Safe and the next Show goes on properly. My Heart and prayers are with with everyone that was injured last night,” he added.
Manchester was left shaken in 2017 after a bombing at a nearby venue during an Ariana Grande concert left 22 people dead and made global headlines.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised,” Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said Monday. “We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital,” Parker added.
Concertgoer Joey Howe, 22, told BBC Radio Manchester the lights came on and Toliver appeared to have been “rushed off stage.”

“I saw a lot of people streaming out and you go into this panic mode and you see a lot of people running out of the venue,” Howe said. He said people were “choking” and there was a “horrible smell” in the arena.
“It was just really distressing scenes and not something you want to see,” he added.
Another fan, Ben Stevenson, told the Manchester Evening News that he was in the standing section of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”
A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a former mayor of Manchester, called the incident “deeply worrying” and said the police would conduct a full investigation.
The venue, which opened in 2024, is due to host American singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

It said in a statement on X that it was “working closely with Greater Manchester Police to identify the cause and action appropriately. Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update.”

title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship off Libya in latest expansion of the war
summary: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.
story: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Ukrainian naval drones had been used in the attack in the Mediterranean a day earlier, which came after Moscow said another of its ships was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea.
Zelenskyy shared footage of the attacks in a post on X, showing drones approaching several vessels followed by massive fireballs.
He said his forces deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones to sink the Russian corvette, Merkury, and hit a transport ship, the Angara, in an “exemplary Ukrainian operation.”

Later, in a separate post on the social media site, he said Ukraine responded “to Russia’s strikes the way it should be done, the way that is effective,” adding: “It is also important that without these ships in those waters, it will be harder for Russia to fuel conflicts and instability in that region as well.”
Ukraine’s Security Service, SBU, said the attacks took place near the Libyan port of Benghazi, some 1,500 miles from the established front lines of the conflict.

It said the corvette “regularly escorted enemy naval convoys” and in particular guarded the Angara cargo ship that was used to move weapons. “Both vessels were legitimate military targets for Ukraine, as they worked directly for Russia’s military capabilities,” the SBU said in a statement on Telegram.

Ukrainian uncrewed boats were delivered to a designated location and launched into the water from a so-called “mother ship,” the SBU said, reaching their targets despite “enemy’s attempts to destroy the Ukrainian drones from the air.” It said the Ka-27 multi-purpose helicopter was on board the corvette and was also sunk.
“The Defence Forces of Ukraine have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea,” the SBU added.
Ukraine noted that the ship was one of Russia’s newest, commissioned only in 2023.

Moscow has noted Zelenskyy’s “statement on this matter,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday when asked about the attacks. He deferred to the Russian Defense Ministry, which was yet to comment.
It’s the latest example of Kyiv launching surprise attacks to hit back against the Kremlin.
But the weekend attack caused fallout in Libya, where local authorities expressed outrage and the United Nations called for an independent probe.

The eastern Libya-based government said Sunday that an explosion took place aboard a Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base. It said the vessel was en route back to Russia and had stopped at the port to refuel and take on supplies.
A comprehensive investigation into the attack will be launched, it said, in coordination with Russian authorities.
